(4) "Whether it is the 2026-11-04 API-only target is unknown" should ask whether the model now served is the one qualified on 2026-11-04 (model root Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4). The alias RM-01 VLM earlier also served the 27B, and probe P1 can show a difference but cannot prove identical weights. Corrections to BL-20261105-1822-project-review-reset-proposed. (5) Scope: "verified bugs" should read "code findings, those marked H re-read at 153b8e6"; nothing in the review is Verified. (6) Decision (a) dropped the tolerance. The revised proposal: a route changes only if it is worse on no column by more than that column's tolerance and better on at least one by more than its tolerance, with symmetric tolerances (quality one accept in six; cost USD 0.02 or 10% of mean settled USD, whichever is larger; public disclosed bytes 10%; labelled bytes zero). (7) Decision (c) made local-first escalation the design. The forced split, where both assists always fire, is now an equal E3 candidate, and the cloud's default role is an owner decision. SearXNG relays each query to upstream engines, which see it. (8) Evidence: the 1,200-word synthesis limit is prompt text only, since the enforced bound is the 8,192-token reply. Plain HTTP to a non-loopback local model also needs the machine-local SOAR_ALLOW_INSECURE_VLLM_HTTP opt-in. "The desktop ships no research ... route" means no staged-research route: desktop general tasks can still research up to three URLs through the agent loop. (9) Changes omitted that docs/README.md also marks the 2026-09-28 review's row as succeeded. (10) Paid exposure: about USD 28.4-28.7 remains on the harness line, not 29.4. The log charges the line USD 3.11-3.44 for H1 and H3 plus 1.15 for Claude, and only 3.56 of that is in registry rows. The proposed caps were incomplete and are revised, none authorized: E2 at most USD 1 for fixtures; E3 USD 20.4 (25 runs, the forced split now with two repeats); E4 USD 20.5 with SearXNG (36 runs, three repeats so that criterion 9 can be measured, with paired retrieval), up to 7.56 more with a keyed search API; E5 assists at most USD 0.75 per task from the weekly public-work line; E6 at most USD 1; E7 USD 1.5. Separately gated is the E4 option, a Manus product baseline with credits worth about USD 45-81 at list and likely USD 80-200 in cash.

Its "likely USD 80-200 in cash" assumed three fixed Manus tiers. Manus lists its USD 20 and USD 40 tiers as "starting from" 4,000 and 8,000 credits and calls the USD 40 tier customizable, so the cash may be about the USD 45-81 list value; USD 80-200 applies only if no intermediate amount exists. Decisions: Corrections to BL-20261105-1357-second-check-corrections-utc-reset: (1) Its Changes say the revised review gives "a quality floor for every E3 route and an outcome for every E3 and E4 result, including ties within tolerance and E4's default and beta levels". That did not hold. In E3 the floor of accepts(D) − 1 applied to every route, and the all-cloud ceiling D, which runs one repeat, meets it trivially, so in a round that was not harness-limited the outcome "no route is eligible" could not occur and D could become the default, which the review's stop list rules out. In E4, two arms at the same level that were equal within every tolerance had no outcome, and the order for choosing E4's cloud-assisted arm could take B or C from a harness-limited or ineligible E3 result before reaching the owner's choice. (2) Its correction (4) should read: the revised review proposes that E3's pre-registered rule picks the cloud's default role, which takes effect once the owner records it. If the round is harness-limited or no route is eligible, no route changes. If more than one eligible route stays unbeaten, because they trade columns or are equal within every tolerance, the owner chooses, and the owner names E4's cloud-assisted arm when E3 cannot. The owner may instead fix the role now (review section 5.10, item 2). All of this is Proposed. (3) Its Changes' "docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md is revised in place for the 54 findings" should read, as review section 8 says, that the review, docs/PLAN.md and that entry, with its validator allowlist row and tests, together apply the fixes for the 54. At 90046a0 the findings behind its corrections (3), (9), (10) and (11) and its UTC reset had changed no review text; correction (10) reaches the review's F5 only in this revision. (4) Its "The header, the direction section and section 8 record both checks" should read that the header and section 8 record both checks. The direction section records neither; its changes cite BL-20261105-2016-correction-direction-and-review-entries for the standing instruction and mark the two further supersessions as readings pending the owner's confirmation. ### BL-20261107-0809-zero-fee-failures-resolve-design -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 1 decided: zero-risk failures resolve `failed`, a settlement sub-code, a deadline guard before priced dispatch, and resolved reader rows in the research producer

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: The decision entry for backlog item 1 of docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.7 (findings A1, A2, A8, B1, D14, F7), recorded before its code as section 5.7 requires for a change to dispatch semantics or a persisted contract. docs/HANDOFF.md's "Start here (2026-11-07)" step 1 orders this work; it is zero-fee code with deterministic tests and needs no approval under PLAN.md section 4, so the implementation follows in the same pull request, and the owner may record otherwise. Three adversarial design reviews (ledger and replay safety; downstream consumers and tests; specification fidelity) passed the design with the changes recorded here.

Decisions: (1) A zero-risk packet (a zero-fee local request or a public GET without a grant or approval, the predicate `broker.request` already applies, now exposed as `zeroRiskDispatch`) never leaves an `unknown` row: every transport diagnostic (`request_timeout`, `cancelled`, `response_oversize`, `transport_failed`, `inactivity_timeout`, `stream_invalid`, beside the already confirmed `connection_failed`, `http_rejected`, `upstream_closed`, `response_interrupted` and `stream_error`) and every settlement diagnostic (`response_or_usage_invalid`, and `fee_settlement_failed`, reachable at a zero reservation only through the store's own check) is confirmed; the row resolves `failed`, or `superseded` when a retry follows, and the broker denies `request_failed`. A priced or cloud packet keeps today's semantics: only a non-dispatch or an error answer is confirmed, everything else stays `unknown` with its reservation pinned and the job blocked. For zero-risk packets only, this supersedes the statements that a timeout "still ends the task without replay" (BL-20261007-0321-pr-c-recoverable-dispatch-design, BL-20261007-0530-pr-c-recoverable-dispatch-implemented) and that `inactivity_timeout` and `stream_invalid` "remain unknown outcomes" (BL-20261007-1045-pr-b-liveness-design); their rationale, that the server may still have produced a result, stands, and the new reading is that a packet re-sendable without cost or side effect loses GPU time only. (2) The retry set is unchanged and now explicit: `connection_failed`, `upstream_closed`, `response_interrupted`, and `http_rejected` or `stream_error` whose recorded status is at least 500 or exactly 429; no status, another 4xx, a timeout, a cancel, an oversize or malformed reply and a settlement failure are never retried (owner decision D4 of 2026-09-29 is unchanged). (3) The settlement diagnostic gains an optional `subcode` from a fixed list (`SETTLEMENT_SUBCODES` in store.ts: the reply decoders' codes, the broker's local-reply checks, the store's fee check, and `other`), recorded on new rows of every destination and never provider text; rows written before the field have none. (4) Finding A8: before each model dispatch the runner and the research pipeline compare the time left with the destination's request timeout; a call that would not be zero-risk is not started when less time remains (the runner ends with the new reason `deadline_before_request`, nothing recorded or sent; the pipeline records it as the stage's `denied` code under `research_request_denied`), so a deadline cut on a first attempt can no longer leave an uncertain row with a pinned reservation; a zero-risk call proceeds, since the deadline resolves its row `failed`. The guard forfeits a priced job's last timeout window (900 s under Heavy; the cloud runs so far finished in about nine minutes of a ninety-minute allowance). A deadline during an Anthropic retry attempt inside one request can still leave an `unknown` row, an accepted residual until section 5.2's S8 sizes calls from the E0 card. (5) On `request_failed` the runner keeps recording `model_request_failed` (reason literal `model_unavailable`) and ends the run paused when a pause was pending (a pause is honoured at the loop top, so this branch needs a concurrent failure), as `cancelled_or_deadline` when its bounded signal is aborted, the job is cancelled or no active time remains, and as resumable `model_unavailable` otherwise; a cancel before the row is committed (`request_cancelled`, finding A5) stays with item 3. (6) Finding D14: the research producer binds every resolved reader-context row: a `superseded` row (the D4 local retry or the Anthropic destination's 429 or 529 retry) and a `failed` row bind as `{id, stage, sha256, status}` with `status` present only on non-settled rows (every existing producer stays byte-identical) and with no response hash or fee, and each stage's calls must equal its rows no retry superseded; `committed` and `unknown` rows still refuse the binding. Today no packet coexists with a failed reader row, because a denied call ends the stage, so the failed-counted rule is reachable only in unit tests; item 7 must reconcile it with the ready-packet check (research-coverage.ts: extraction calls equal chunk attempts, invalid replies stay below calls) before a stage may continue after a failed call.

Changes: Planned in this pull request: store.ts (`isConfirmedAbort`, `isRetryableAbort`, `SETTLEMENT_SUBCODES`, the schema field), broker.ts (`zeroRiskDispatch`, `requestTimeoutMs`, the sub-code, comments), model.ts (`DEADLINE_BEFORE_REQUEST_STOP`, `deadlineRefuses`), runner.ts (the guard, the stop mapping, the fetch-failure observation text, which the prompt protocol hash does not cover), research-pipeline.ts (`deadlineMs`), session.ts (passes the session deadline), research-producer.ts (resolved bindings), controller.ts (the fixed reason and its status mapping; the sub-code beside an uncertain settlement's description). Recorded values that change downstream: a zero-risk public fetch that times out, is cut or is oversize reaches the model as `public_fetch_failed` and the task continues, instead of ending `unresolved_dispatch_no_replay`; the headless driver's result reason and the registry's `terminalCause` read `model_unavailable`, `cancelled_or_deadline` or `research_request_denied` where they read `runtime_failure_progress_preserved` or `research_cancelled` beside an unknown row; a paused or cancelled research stage resumes to `research_stage_not_replayed` instead of `unresolved_dispatch_no_replay` (finding A7 stands); the harness loop stops on `loop_stage_failed_dispatch` instead of `loop_stage_unresolved_dispatch` until item 11 admits resolved zero-fee rows. Tests that pinned the old behaviour are rewritten, not deleted, and finding D14 is reproduced by a deterministic session test before the fix.

Evidence: Finding D14 reproduced at 456344e before any fix: a research stage whose extraction call the broker retried once (the socket cut after dispatch on a recoverable destination) completed its packet, and `createResearchProducer` threw `research_producer_unsettled_receipt` out of `GeneralAgentSession.run` (tests/unit/private-agent-research-session.test.ts, the D14 case). The three design reviews' findings are applied above: the public-fetch consumer, the broker-owned zero-risk predicate for the guard, the superseded PR-B and PR-C statements, the Anthropic and public-DNS tests, the vacuous failed-count rule, the pause semantics, and the E1 split below.

Failures or blockers: None in recording. The runner's pre-commit `request_cancelled` path (finding A5) and the desktop's resume reasons (finding A6) stay as they are until items 3 and 6.

Limitations and non-claims: This entry decides; nothing is implemented or verified by it. E1's gate clause "local work continues after a cloud UNKNOWN" belongs to item 10's assist-purpose exception, not to item 1, which serves E1's other clauses (zero zero-fee UNKNOWN rows, a retried stage reaches the writer, cancellation still stops the stage). A priced local reply that fails validation stays `unknown` (finding A2's wider wording yields to item 1's zero-risk scope). A process crash between commit and close still leaves a `committed` row that blocks the ledger and counts as an unknown dispatch in the harness. Cloud and consultant dispatch semantics are otherwise unchanged; items 8 (concurrent zero-risk dispatch), 10 and 11 are out of scope.

Paid exposure: None. Zero SOAR model requests and zero envelope spend.

Next gate: The implementation with deterministic tests in this pull request and its `Implemented` entry; then CI green and a merge per the handoff's step 1.

References: docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 4 rows A1, A2, A8, B1, D14 and section 5.7 item 1; docs/HANDOFF.md "Start here (2026-11-07)"; BL-20261107-0650-owner-decisions-review-items-2-5; BL-20261107-0718-correction-owner-decisions-record; BL-20261007-0321-pr-c-recoverable-dispatch-design; BL-20261007-0530-pr-c-recoverable-dispatch-implemented; BL-20261007-1045-pr-b-liveness-design; BL-20261030-0620-claude-cloud-adapter-design; docs/PLAN.md section 4 and decision D4.


### BL-20261107-0812-zero-fee-failures-resolve-implemented -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 1 implemented: zero-risk failures resolve `failed`, settlement sub-codes, the deadline guard before priced dispatch, and resolved reader rows bound by the research producer

Status: `Implemented`

Scope or hypothesis: Implement BL-20261107-0809-zero-fee-failures-resolve-design as decided, with deterministic tests, in pull request branch `fix/zero-fee-failures-resolve` based on `claude/great-meitner-kri52m`. Hypothesis: with these changes a zero-fee local request or an ungranted public GET can no longer leave an `unknown` row, a research stage whose call the broker retried still reaches the writer, and a cancel, pause or deadline during a zero-fee call ends the run as such with its progress preserved.

Decisions: None new beyond the design entry. Two details fixed in code: a settlement failure whose exception is not one of the listed codes (for example the decoder's TypeError on an invalid UTF-8 stream) records `subcode: other`; and the runner's `public_fetch_failed` observation now says the request "failed, timed out or was cut before a usable reply arrived, and it is not retried", since a resolved zero-risk fetch failure is not retried and was previously described as exhausting "the permitted attempts". The prompt protocol hash does not cover that text, so every paused task resumes under its recorded identity.

Changes: src/main/private-agent/store.ts: `isConfirmedAbort` confirms every failure of a zero-risk packet; `isRetryableAbort` is the explicit transient list; `SETTLEMENT_SUBCODES`, `settlementSubcode()` and the optional `subcode` on the settlement diagnostic. broker.ts: `zeroRiskDispatch()` (also used by `request()`), `requestTimeoutMs()`, the sub-code on settlement failures, comments. model.ts: `DEADLINE_BEFORE_REQUEST_STOP`, `PrivateAgentModel.deadlineRefuses()`. runner.ts: the pre-dispatch guard before `model_started`; `request_failed` and the Anthropic retry-wait cancel share one mapping (paused, `cancelled_or_deadline`, or `model_unavailable`); the fetch-failure text. research-pipeline.ts: optional `deadlineMs` and the guard in `call()`. session.ts: passes the session deadline to the pipeline. research-producer.ts: resolved rows bind with `status`, settled rows unchanged, calls counted against unsuperseded rows. general-tasks/controller.ts: the `deadline_before_request` fixed reason and status mapping; the sub-code beside an uncertain settlement's description. Tests rewritten for the new contract: tests/integration/private-agent-broker.test.ts (plus a new zero-risk describe), private-agent-broker-anthropic.test.ts (settlement key sets gain `subcode`), private-agent-flash-next.test.ts (twenty validation failures now resolve `failed` with their sub-code), tests/unit/private-agent-public-dns.test.ts (a cut lookup on a zero-risk GET resolves `failed`), private-agent-public-research.test.ts (a failed zero-risk fetch becomes an observation and the task continues), private-agent-research-seed.test.ts (superseded rows uncounted, local and Anthropic-shaped; a genuine failed row counted; forged rows refused; the seed loader path), private-agent-research-session.test.ts (the D14 reproduction, now passing), private-agent-research-pipeline.test.ts and private-agent-runner-budget.test.ts (the deadline guard; cancel, deadline, pause and retry-wait mappings).

### BL-20261107-0839-assist-purpose-exception-design -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 10, week 1: the assist-purpose exception decided for the ledger, the broker, the pre-checks, the research producer and the harness loop

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: The decision entry for the week-1 part of backlog item 10 of docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.7, the assist-purpose exception that section 5.2 "Escalation" places in four places (the session, runner and controller pre-checks; `store.commit`; the research producer's receipt binding; the harness loop's stage checks), recorded before its code because it changes dispatch semantics and persisted contracts. It is based on backlog item 1 (BL-20261107-0809-zero-fee-failures-resolve-design, PR #37), after which the only `unknown` rows a research job can hold are priced or cloud rows. The assist wrapper itself (T1 and T2 packets, firing policies, fallback lists) is item 10's later part; E1 tests the exception. Three adversarial design reviews (ledger and replay safety; downstream consumers and tests; specification fidelity) passed the design with the changes recorded here. The handoff's step 1 orders this work; it is zero-fee code with deterministic tests and needs no approval under PLAN.md section 4, so the implementation follows in the same pull request; the owner may record otherwise.

Decisions: (1) Two fixed purposes name the sealed cloud one-shots, `research plan assist` and `research synthesis assist`, in a new module `src/main/private-agent/dispatch-purposes.ts` with `isAssistDispatch` and `assistStage`; `isBlockingDispatch(row, ownContextId)` lives in store.ts beside `isResolvedDispatch`; scripts/registry-row.py mirrors the strings and a test keeps them equal. They are distinct from every local stage purpose, so a local plan or synthesis row is never exempted. (2) An assist purpose is admitted only on a `cloud_model` destination, refused in the broker's `packet()` (so in `preview()` and `request()`) with `assist_destination_invalid`: the purpose exempts a row from the unresolved rule and the harness stops, so a priced local or web row can never carry it. (3) Ledger admission in `store.commit`, inside its transaction: any `committed` row and any `unknown` row of another purpose block every dispatch, as today (`private_agent_unresolved_dispatch`); when the only unresolved rows are `unknown` assist rows, a dispatch of another purpose is admitted and an assist dispatch is refused with `private_agent_assist_after_unknown`. This is the ledger's own guarantee for writers other than the broker; the exposure sum is unchanged, so the skipped assist's reservation stays pinned for the job's life. (4) Section 5.2's "after an UNKNOWN, no further cloud call is made in the job": the broker's commit-time validator refuses every grant-free dispatch to a `cloud_model` destination while the job holds an `unknown` assist row, whatever the purpose (`cloud_after_assist_unknown`), so a second assist and a cloud writer call are both refused; through the broker this fires before (3). A grant-backed call, the owner's exact-packet consultation, is not refused here, because a refusal before its row exists would leave the consultation `uncertain` and block resume (consultation.ts records the attempt before dispatch); item 1's reading that consultant dispatch semantics are unchanged still holds, and item 13 must decide where a consultation after a skipped assist is declined (recommended: at proposal or approval, as a disclosed fallback) before the desktop issues assists. (5) The pre-checks use `isBlockingDispatch(row, privateContextId)` together with the existing entailment exemption: the session before and after the reading stage and before submission, the runner's `unsettledDispatch` (its own context), and the controller's `uncertain()`; an `unknown` assist row in another context than the writer's, the reading stage's, blocks nothing, while one in the writer's own context, which no producer binds, still blocks. The controller's `unknownReason` describes the last blocking unknown row, never a skipped assist. The research-stage replay refusal (`research_stage_not_replayed`) is unchanged, and the desktop issues no assist before item 13. (6) The research producer binds every assist row of the reader context to the stage its purpose names, as `{id, stage, sha256, role: "assist"}` plus `status` when not settled; `role` and `status` are absent on local rows, so every existing producer is byte-identical. A settled assist is one of its stage's calls, so a forced-split plan or synthesis stage whose only call is its assist passes the per-stage count; a skipped (`unknown`), failed or superseded assist binds uncounted, since a stage's `calls` are its replies and such a row has none. An `unknown` row is admitted only with an assist purpose, a `committed` row never, and a non-settled row carries no response hash or fee. This keeps the ready-packet validator's bounds (calls within the frozen budget, plan attempts equal to plan calls, invalid replies below calls) and the protocol hash unchanged. An `unknown` row is terminal (`store.close` touches only committed rows), so the binding's hash is stable across resume and seeding. "Resolved as skipped" therefore means an `unknown` row exempted by its purpose, never closed, its reservation pinned; no new `DispatchStatus` is introduced. (7) The stage summary's assist record is not defined here: item 10's wrapper entry defines it, and it must carry the attempts, the outcome (settled, skipped or failed) and the usage per assist, cache-write tokens included, so E3's zero-cache-write condition is checkable from the stage event and the registry; it must keep `calls` as replies. The local-first shapes (two local calls plus one assist) need item 7(c)'s budgets and the protocol bump they imply. (8) The harness: `summarizeRun` reports `assistSkippedDispatches` (unknown assist rows) and `assistFailedDispatches` (failed assist rows) and excludes both from `unknownDispatches` and `failedDispatches`; a `committed` assist row stays unresolved; the loop's totals, the registry row and docs/experiments/README.md gain the two columns; LOOP_VERSION stays 1 (additive keys); a skipped assist is not a model call and its pinned reservation is not in `usd` until item 11 adds reserved USD. The loop's stage checks then admit a sample whose assist was skipped or failed into the host fallback, while a zero-fee `failed` row still stops the loop until item 11. (9) Out of scope: the wrapper, item 7(c)'s host fallbacks, item 11, item 13's toggle and badge.

Changes: Planned in this pull request: dispatch-purposes.ts (new); store.ts (`isBlockingDispatch`, the commit rule, the new code); broker.ts (the destination binding in `packet()`, the grant-free cloud refusal in the commit validator); session.ts, runner.ts and general-tasks/controller.ts (the pre-check predicates; `unknownReason`); research-producer.ts (the assist variants and the count rule); selection.ts, scripts/phase4-loop.ts, scripts/registry-row.py and docs/experiments/README.md (the two counts). Tests: a purposes unit test, broker and store integration tests for (2), (3) and (4), runner and controller tests for (5), producer and seed-loader tests for (6), selection, loop and registry tests for (8).

Evidence: The three reviews' findings are applied: the count rule narrowed to settled assists after the reviewers showed that counting a skipped or failed assist as a call fails the ready-packet validator's stage bounds and plan-attempt rule (research-coverage.ts, research-plan.ts) outside the forced split; the cloud refusal narrowed to grant-free dispatch after the consultation path's uncertain state was traced (consultation.ts, runner.ts, controller.ts); the exemption scoped to rows outside the writer's context; the stage-summary record deferred to the wrapper with E3's cache-write requirement named; the destination binding placed in `packet()`; the store code shown reachable only outside the broker; the registry README told to document every dispatch column; LOOP_VERSION kept. E1's clause "local work continues after a cloud UNKNOWN" is proved here at the store, broker, runner, controller, producer and loop levels with injected rows; its end-to-end proof needs the wrapper.

Failures or blockers: None in recording. A desktop consultation after a skipped assist is an open item-13 question (see decision 4); a `committed` assist row, a crash mid-dispatch, still blocks the job.

Limitations and non-claims: This entry decides; nothing is implemented or verified by it. No cloud, model or paid call is involved. The exemption does not run end to end until the wrapper dispatches assists; the split arm still sends cloud plan and synthesis under the plain stage purposes and keeps today's blocking semantics until the wrapper switches it. Finding A1's remaining cloud `unknown` rows of other purposes keep their at-most-once semantics and block the job, as item 1 recorded.

Paid exposure: None. Zero SOAR model requests and zero envelope spend.

Next gate: The implementation with deterministic tests in this pull request, based on PR #37, and its `Implemented` entry; then CI green and a merge; then items 3 and 4, and item 10's wrapper with the stage-summary record of decision 7.

References: docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.2 (Escalation, Forced split, Caching) and section 5.7 items 7(c), 10, 11 and 13; docs/HANDOFF.md "Start here (2026-11-07)"; BL-20261107-0809-zero-fee-failures-resolve-design; BL-20261107-0812-zero-fee-failures-resolve-implemented; BL-20261107-0650-owner-decisions-review-items-2-5; BL-20261026-1831-h4-select-and-repair-design (the loop's stop rule this entry relaxes for assist rows).

### BL-20261107-0859-label-keyed-diagnostics-design -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 4 decided: diagnostics keyed on label, raw rejected replies retained only for public or synthetic contexts, hashes only for labelled ones

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: The decision entry for backlog item 4 of docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.7 (finding F3 of section 3 and rows B3, B4 and B6 of section 4), recorded before its code as section 5.7 requires, because it decides where model text may be written and where it never may. It is based on backlog item 10's week-1 branch `fix/assist-purpose-exception` (PR #38) on top of item 1 (PR #37): the broker's settlement `subcode` (B1) is item 1's and is not redone here, and `runtime_failure.brokerCode` (B2) and the runner belong to item 3, which another branch edits concurrently. It is zero-fee code with deterministic tests and needs no approval under PLAN.md section 4, so the implementation follows in the same pull request; the owner may record otherwise, in particular on the two open questions below.

Decisions: (1) The retention policy is a pure function of the persisted context, never of a surface or a command-line flag: `diagnosticRetention(context)` in contracts.ts returns `"raw"` iff `syntheticContext(context)` holds, that is every source is `public`, or `private` with the synthetic attestation, and `"hash_only"` otherwise; one credential source or one private, non-synthetic source makes the whole context hash-only. Context taint is monotonic (store.addSources only adds sources), so a labelled job can never become raw later, while a raw job becomes hash-only the moment a labelled source joins it. "Public or synthetic" therefore means `syntheticContext` as the code already defines it, which admits the headless driver's synthetic-attested private sources and the desktop's URL-backed public tasks; the owner may narrow it to `!restrictedContext` (purely public sources), in which case the harness retains nothing. (2) The pipeline gains an optional `diagnostics` sink, called for every rejected or truncated settled reply of the four stages with `{ stage, ordinal, purpose, replyContentSha256, replyBytes, truncated, content, reasons }`, where `reasons` are the fixed codes and schema paths each stage already computes (for the planner the complete validation list as code and path pairs, unbounded, beside the bounded attempt record) and never provider or model text beyond `content` itself. Only rejected and truncated replies are retained, which is what F3 needs; retaining every reply is E0's fixture work (item 5). Reasoning text is never retained: flash-next-reply.ts deletes it at the transport, and this entry does not reopen that. A denied call has no reply and retains nothing. (3) Nothing protocol-bound changes: `RESEARCH_PLAN_DIAGNOSTIC_POLICY`, `ResearchPlanAttemptSchema`, `LIMITS`, every constant inside `researchProtocolSha256`, `ResearchStageCounts`, summary.json, coverage.json, the `research_stage` event and the registry row stay hash-only for every label; a test pins `researchProtocolSha256()` to its value at the base commit, 3453710315d7226ea4d6195ec7401d000f86c5b0d9afa9839a801d5c6d391262, and a guard test checks that summary stage rows carry no key outside the documented set and no reply text. (4) The session accepts an optional `research.diagnostics` sink and forwards it to the pipeline only when `diagnosticRetention(store.context(readerContextId)) === "raw"` at the moment of the call; the sink is no part of the session identity; the desktop controller passes none, so the desktop is byte-identical and retains nothing. (5) Raw text may be written in exactly one place: the headless driver's ignored run directory, under `<output-directory>/diagnostics/`, one file per entry named by `replyContentSha256`, mode 0o600, beside a hashes-only `manifest.json` (stage, ordinal, purpose, sha256, bytes, truncated, reasons; no content), and only when the operator passes the new `--retain-diagnostics true` flag with `--pipeline research`. The driver refuses the flag unless `git check-ignore` reports the output directory ignored, so retained text can never sit in a tracked path, and the freeze records `diagnosticsRetained: true`, a boolean only. Raw text never goes into events, receipts, summary.json, coverage.json, result.json, the registry or the desktop store. (6) Harness codes (B6): the loop writes the full caught error, name and message, to `errors.txt` under the loop directory while `loop.json`'s `failure` stays a code; research-seed.ts gains `researchTransferStatus(runDirectory)`, the snapshot fingerprint or the snake_case refusal code (an exception that is not a code maps to `research_seed_load_failed`), with `researchTransferSnapshot`'s null contract unchanged; the loop records that code in its log and as `seedRefusal` on `selected.final` when sample a leaves no packet to seed from (an additive key; LOOP_VERSION stays 1). (7) Out of scope: B3's outcome-reason change (the exact broker code already survives in the `research_stage` event's `denied` field), the runner (item 3), desktop retention, every-reply retention, reasoning text, and the driver's top-level catch text.

Changes: Planned in this pull request: contracts.ts (`diagnosticRetention`); research-plan.ts (the complete issue list returned beside the unchanged attempt record); research-pipeline.ts (`ResearchDiagnostic`, the optional sink, the per-stage reasons); session.ts (the gated forward); research-diagnostics.ts (new: the file sink and the git-ignore check, harness only); scripts/private-agent-local-screen.ts (the flag, the sink, the freeze boolean); scripts/phase4-loop.ts (`errors.txt`, the transfer status, `seedRefusal`); research-seed.ts (`researchTransferStatus`). Tests: the retention predicate with the store's monotonic taint; the pipeline sink across the four stages with byte-identical files and the pinned protocol hash; the planner's complete issue list; the session's gated forward on a synthetic-attested and a labelled job; the file sink and the ignore check against a temporary git repository; the loop's side file and the seed loader's codes.

Evidence: None yet; this entry decides. The reading that `syntheticContext` is the only label in code today, that the harness classifies every input source private with `synthetic: true` under its attestation (session.ts, `context()`), that `.soar/` is ignored and that `git check-ignore` reports a not yet created path under it as ignored, is from the code at 6f735fa and a shell check in the worktree.

Failures or blockers: None in recording. Two open questions for the owner: whether "public or synthetic" should mean `syntheticContext` (decision 1) or purely public sources; and whether reasoning text may ever be retained for synthetic contexts (the default here is never).

Limitations and non-claims: This entry decides; nothing is implemented or verified by it. No model, endpoint, Docker container or paid call is involved. Retention binds to a self-declared attestation (review rows C1 and C4): a mislabelled synthetic task retains its rejected replies as any synthetic task does. The file sink is file-only and off by default, so it changes no persisted contract; the `seedRefusal` key and the freeze boolean are additive.

Paid exposure: None. Zero SOAR model requests and zero envelope spend.

Next gate: The implementation with deterministic tests in this pull request and its `Implemented` entry; then CI green and a merge after PR #38.

### BL-20261107-0923-label-keyed-diagnostics-implemented -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 4 implemented: diagnostics keyed on label, the pipeline's optional sink, the session's label gate, the headless driver's file sink behind `--retain-diagnostics`, and the harness codes

Status: `Implemented`

Scope or hypothesis: Implement BL-20261107-0859-label-keyed-diagnostics-design as decided, with deterministic tests, on branch `feat/label-keyed-diagnostics` based on `fix/assist-purpose-exception` (PR #38, backlog item 10 week 1, itself on PR #37). Hypothesis: with these changes a rejected or truncated reading-stage reply and its complete validation reasons can be kept, as files in the headless driver's ignored run directory and nowhere else, exactly when the reader context is wholly public or synthetic-attested, while every persisted record stays hash-only for every label and the frozen research protocol is unchanged.

Decisions: None new beyond the design entry. Four details fixed in code: (1) the file sink never fails a run: a write failure is counted in the manifest (`writeFailures`) and the run goes on; the sink creates `diagnostics/` and an empty manifest when the driver starts, so a run that rejected nothing still shows retention was on; a reply is written once however often its content recurs, under the sha256 of its bytes, which equals the pipeline's `replyContentSha256`. (2) The driver's command line admits `--retain-diagnostics true` only beside `--pipeline research`, while `runLocalArtifactScreen` accepts the flag on a seeded run (the loop strips the pipeline for b and the repair), runs the git-ignore check and builds no sink there. (3) The guard test found eight integer counts that `summarizeIndexEntries` has always assigned onto the index stage row beyond `ResearchStageCounts` (`sourcesModelRepaired`, `sourcesModelUnattempted`, `invalidJsonReplies`, `invalidSchemaReplies`, `unexpectedRows`, `duplicateExpectedIds`, `missingSources`, `emptyGists`); the test documents them and checks that every stage value is a count, a fixed code, the usage counts or a schema-valid plan attempt; the interface is left unchanged. (4) Zod schema failures in extraction and synthesis replies reach the sink as `schema_<zod code>` with paths reduced to known field names and indexes (`?` otherwise), so an unknown key's name never leaves the pipeline.

### BL-20261107-0924-stop-bricking-tasks-design -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 3 decided: workspace capture inside the handled flow, a lister that skips and reports, output overflow bounded without destroying the container, pre-dispatch broker denials recorded as not dispatched, and specific tool error codes

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: The decision entry for backlog item 3 of docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.7, "Stop bricking tasks" (findings A3, A4, A5 and B5 of section 4, and the `runtime_failure` broker code of B2), recorded before its code because it changes persisted events and dispatch classification. It is based on backlog items 1 and 10 (BL-20261107-0812-zero-fee-failures-resolve-implemented, BL-20261107-0842-assist-purpose-exception-implemented; PRs #37 and #38), whose `request_failed` mapping and `isBlockingDispatch` predicate the runner keeps. Hypothesis: with these changes an ordinary workspace (a symlink, a virtual environment, a clone with more than 1,024 files, a file over 64 MiB), a chatty command, a broker refusal before any row exists, or a tool error no longer leaves a `tool_started` or `model_started` unmatched, so no task ends in `unresolved_operation_no_replay` for any of those reasons, and the model receives a fixed repair signal instead of one generic error. The owner fixed decisions A to F below in the task brief; this entry records them as proposed, with the refinements marked, so the owner can override. Zero-fee code with deterministic tests; no approval is needed under PLAN.md section 4, so the implementation follows in the same pull request.

Decisions: (A, finding A3) Every workspace capture runs inside handled flow. After an action, a capture failure no longer reaches the outer catch: the runner still records the `checkpoint` event (carrying the prior snapshot unchanged, since progress.ts requires a checkpoint immediately before every retained execute's `tool_finished`) and the `tool_finished` event, closing the operation; the event gains an optional host-authored `captureFailure: { code }` with `code` from a fixed set (`sandbox_<code>` for the nine SandboxError codes, `checkpoint_write_failed` for a failure of the checkpoint store, `capture_failed` for anything else), the sandbox is closed if still live and recreated from the last checkpoint, and the run continues. Refinement of A: `tool_finished.output` keeps the action's own result in every case (so a retained execute's output stays the observation module's exact rendering, a failed execute's output stays its fixed error object, and an edit's or fetch's result is not overwritten), and the host-authored feedback `{ error: "workspace_capture_failed", code, completed: false, actionInvoked: true, instruction }`, which tells the model that every workspace change since the last checkpoint, this action's included, was not retained, travels as a user message right after the tool result, generated deterministically from the event on the live path and on every replay, as steering and nudge messages already do; only a `finish` whose capture failed has the capture failure as its output (`{ complete: false, error: "workspace_capture_failed", code }`), since no verification ran. A second consecutive capture failure in one run still records `tool_finished`, then records `runtime_failure` with the original error's code and ends `runtime_failure_progress_preserved`, so the run ends as today but the operation is closed and a later run resumes from the last checkpoint; the counter is per run and resets on a successful capture. The pre-stop recheck capture (before `tool_started`, when a warned execute is repeated) is inconclusive on failure: the sandbox is recreated from the last checkpoint and the action runs against it, which records `tool_started` and keeps `hasUnresolvedExecutionProgressAction` sound; the action's `tool_finished` records it as `recheckCaptureFailure: { code }` and the notice says the recheck could not run. The finish capture's failure skips verification and is handled like any action's. The allowance-validation capture's failure records `host_validation_finished` with `passed: false`, `checks: []`, the required paths missing from the prior snapshot and `captureFailure: { code }`, and the run ends `bounded_allowance_exhausted`; a later run returns `host_validation_not_replayed`, as after any finished validation, never `unresolved_operation_no_replay`. (B) The lister (`LIST_FILES` in sandbox.ts) walks in sorted order, never follows a link, and reports instead of dying: a symlink, a multi-link file, a FIFO, socket or device, a file over 64 MiB and an entry whose name the host path rule refuses are omitted with the fixed reasons `symlink`, `hard_link`, `special`, `oversize` and `name_invalid` (a refinement: an odd model-created name is not a traversal, so it loses only itself; `die()`, exit 53, remains for the walk's own failure, which the host still maps to `unsafe_file`); regular files beyond the 1,024-file cap are omitted with reason `cap`, and when more than 4,096 entries have been seen the walk stops and the report says it is incomplete. The reply carries each kept file's size, up to 32 omitted paths (workspace-relative names the model already knows) and the count per reason; the host parser refuses any other shape as `unsafe_file`. The runner's `capture()` omits further files beyond the 128 MiB total with reason `total_cap` instead of throwing, and a non-empty omission report is recorded on the action's `tool_finished` as `captureOmitted: { total, reasons, paths, complete }` and reaches the model in the same host notice. (C, finding A4) Mechanism chosen: host-side truncation. The Docker client's collector, for `execute` only, keeps the first 256 KiB of stdout and stderr together in arrival order (cutting the chunk that crosses the cap), discards the rest while staying attached, and lets the command run to its own end or to the in-container timeout, so the exit code is the command's own and the container stays usable; every other Docker call keeps failing closed on overflow. The cut is recorded as a fixed `[host]` note appended to stderr, exactly as the in-container timeout already is, so the observation blob's strict schema and progress.ts's result hash are unchanged, and the model's rendering of such a result is the observation module's excerpt with `truncated: true`, which makes the system prompt's bounded-excerpt promise true without changing its text. In-container bounding was rejected because `head -c` changes the command's exit and a tmpfs redirect meets the 64 MiB `fsize` limit, and an in-container kill on overflow was rejected as racy (the Docker client cannot address the exec's process group); the cost is that a command printing without end runs until the existing 180 s command timeout. (D, finding A5) Every BrokerError the broker throws before a row exists and the runner recognises is recorded as provably not dispatched with one generic strict marker: `model_request_not_dispatched` with `reason: "broker_denied"`, `dispatched: false` and `code` from the fixed enum `request_cancelled`, `packet_scan_failed`, `packet_scan_incomplete_or_blocked`, `packet_size_exceeded`, `destination_missing`, `unresolved_dispatch` (the sixth-listed is an extension of the brief's five: a blocked scan on a cloud packet is as pre-commit and as deterministic as a size excess and otherwise bricks the task). The store's `private_agent_unresolved_dispatch` is wrapped by the broker as `BrokerError("unresolved_dispatch")`; `BrokerError` gains an optional fixed `details: { bodyBytes, limitBytes }` that the broker attaches to `packet_size_exceeded` when the body, not the URL, exceeds the destination's cap. model.ts gains `modelRequestBrokerDenied` in the pattern of `modelRequestSizeStop`, and `hasInvalidModelRequestSizeStop`, the runner's resume checks and the controller's `uncertain()` accept the new marker. Run outcomes: `request_cancelled` ends paused when a pause was pending, otherwise `cancelled_or_deadline`; `packet_scan_failed` ends with the new resumable reason `packet_scan_unavailable`; `packet_size_exceeded` with details records the existing size-stop marker and ends `request_body_size_exceeded`, without details the generic marker and the new non-resumable reason `model_request_denied`; `packet_scan_incomplete_or_blocked` and `destination_missing` end `model_request_denied`; `unresolved_dispatch` ends `unresolved_dispatch_no_replay`. A resumed run with a `model_request_denied` marker in its history ends `model_request_denied` again, as the size stop does. Every other BrokerError (the policy refusals of `packet()` and `eligible()`, which the desktop's local route cannot raise, and `transport_or_settlement_unknown`) is rethrown as today. (E, finding B5) The action catch returns a fixed table of host-authored error objects keyed on code, in a new module `tool-errors.ts` shared with the observation verifier: `tool_unknown`, `destination_denied`, `consultation_unavailable`, `observation_not_authorized`, `observation_range_invalid` (added: an offset past the stream's end), `path_invalid` (an edit tool's path the sandbox refuses), `sandbox_<code>` for the nine sandbox codes with `actionInvoked` stated only where the host knows it (false for `invalid_input`, `busy` and `unusable`, true for `command_timeout`, absent otherwise), and the existing `public_fetch_limit_reached` and `public_fetch_failed` objects unchanged; each carries a fixed instruction and never a message, path or provider text, and the generic `action_failed_or_not_permitted` remains the fallback for an unclassified error. The observation verifier's `validateFailure` accepts, for an execute whose capture is `unavailable`, the generic object or any `sandbox_<code>` object, and for a refused `read_observation` the generic, `observation_not_authorized` or `observation_range_invalid`, still byte for byte, and still rejects free text, extra keys and a true `allowanceFinalizationEligible`. None of the new objects, notices or notes is bound into `promptProtocol`: binding would move `promptProtocolSha256`, fail the golden pin and make every paused task end `runtime_contract_drift`; the current generic and fetch-failure objects are equally unbound. (F, finding B2) The `runtime_failure` event gains `brokerCode` with the broker's fixed code when the error is a BrokerError; `code` keeps `error.name` otherwise. The controller maps `packet_scan_unavailable` as resumable with a fixed text and `model_request_denied` as a non-resumable fixed text. Persisted-event changes, all additive: `tool_finished.captureFailure`, `tool_finished.recheckCaptureFailure`, `tool_finished.captureOmitted`, `host_validation_finished.captureFailure`, the `broker_denied` marker and its code enum, the run reasons `packet_scan_unavailable` and `model_request_denied`, `runtime_failure.brokerCode`, and the `[host]` overflow note inside a retained blob's stderr; every event written so far is byte-identical, and `promptProtocolSha256` and the identity pins do not move.

Changes: Planned in this pull request on branch `fix/stop-bricking-tasks`, based on `fix/assist-purpose-exception`: sandbox.ts (the sorted, reporting lister with sizes; the structured `listFiles()` reply and its parser; the `execute`-only truncating collector and the `[host]` overflow note); runner.ts (a `captureCheckpoint` helper that never throws; the capture-failure handling at the action, pre-stop, finish and allowance captures; the sandbox recreation; the omission report; the host notice on the live path and on replay; the broker-denial branch; the tool error table; `brokerCode`); tool-errors.ts (new); observations.ts (the acceptance set; the `read_observation` errors typed); model.ts (`BROKER_DENIED_STOP`, the code enum, `modelRequestBrokerDenied`, the join in `hasInvalidModelRequestSizeStop`); broker.ts (`details`, the `unresolved_dispatch` wrap); general-tasks/controller.ts (the two fixed reasons, the status mapping, `canResume`, `uncertain()`, the event summary). Tests: tests/unit/private-agent-runner-budget.test.ts (capture failure continues and completes; two consecutive failures end as today with the operation closed and the next run resuming; the pre-stop recheck test rewritten from refusing replay to running the action; finish and allowance capture failures; the omission report; each broker denial code's marker, outcome and second run; each tool error object; `brokerCode`); tests/unit/private-agent-sandbox.test.ts (the lister script run under the machine's python3 against a temporary workspace with a symlink, a hard link, a FIFO, a sparse oversize file and an odd name; the reply parser's refusals; the truncating collector); tests/unit/private-agent-observations.test.ts (the acceptance set); tests/unit/private-agent-model-size.test.ts (the marker join); tests/unit/private-agent-public-research.test.ts (`destination_denied`); tests/unit/general-task-controller.test.ts (the two reasons); tests/integration/private-agent-sandbox.test.ts rewritten to the new contract (omitted links and bounded overflow with a usable container), which only a Docker run can prove.

Evidence: The four bricking paths were re-read at 6f735fa: runner.ts lines 536, 628, 670 and 701 capture outside any handler and the outer catch at 716-720 records only a class; sandbox.ts lines 202-225 die on any link or oversize entry and 97-99 fail the whole exec on overflow, which `operation()` turns into a closed container; the broker's `request_cancelled`, `packet_scan_failed`, `packet_scan_incomplete_or_blocked`, `packet_size_exceeded`, `destination_missing` and the store's `private_agent_unresolved_dispatch` all arise before `store.commit` inserts a row and reach the runner's rethrow at 492; the catch at 645-660 returns the generic object for `tool_unknown`, `destination_denied`, `consultation_unavailable`, `observation_not_authorized`, `observation_range_invalid` and every SandboxError. The tests that pin the old behaviour (runner-budget 281-292, 612-618, 947-951 and 1012; observations 148-162; the Docker-gated sandbox cases 139-149 and 178-184) are named so the Implemented entry can show which were rewritten. The read-only code map prepared for this item was checked line by line and agrees, except that it predates items 1 and 10.

Failures or blockers: None in recording. This session cannot run Docker, the owned model or the Electron end-to-end suite, so the sandbox integration tests will be rewritten but not run here.

Limitations and non-claims: This entry decides; nothing is implemented or verified by it. The lister's and collector's container behaviour is proved here only by running the lister script under the host's python3 on a temporary directory and by unit tests of the host-side parser and collector; the Docker-gated suite stays the live proof. A capture failure whose sandbox recreation itself fails still ends `runtime_failure_progress_preserved`, now with the operation closed. Pre-commit policy refusals outside the six codes keep today's outcome. Resumability of `runtime_failure_progress_preserved` and the other reasons in the desktop is backlog item 6; richer diagnostics beyond `brokerCode` are item 4. Nothing here measures product quality or touches a live model or a paid destination.

### BL-20261107-0936-stop-bricking-tasks-implemented -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 3 implemented: capture inside the handled flow, the reporting lister, bounded output without destroying the container, broker denials recorded as not dispatched, specific tool error codes, and the broker code on runtime failures

Status: `Implemented`

Scope or hypothesis: Implement BL-20261107-0924-stop-bricking-tasks-design as decided, with deterministic tests, on branch `fix/stop-bricking-tasks` based on `fix/assist-purpose-exception` (PR #38, itself on PR #37). Hypothesis: with these changes a workspace capture failure, a lister that meets a link or an oversize file, a command whose output exceeds 256 KiB, a broker refusal before any row exists, and a tool error the model can repair no longer end a task in `unresolved_operation_no_replay`, and the model receives a fixed code for each.

Decisions: None new beyond the design entry. Six details fixed in code: (1) the tool error table gains a tenth host code the design entry did not name, `execution_context_unavailable`, for an action whose container could not be recreated before it ran (nothing invoked), which the observation verifier accepts for a not-invoked execute or read beside the argument feedback; it exists because the recreation after an inconclusive recheck happens inside the handled flow, after `tool_started`, so that a failed recreation closes the operation instead of leaving the warned response unresolved. (2) A `finish` whose verifier or whose container recreation threw now records the sandbox code as its result and continues from the frozen snapshot, where before the `verification_or_cleanup_incomplete` throw left `tool_started` unmatched; the allowance path keeps its no-replay stop for a verifier failure, as its existing test pins. (3) The second-consecutive-failure rule counts a recheck failure and its own action's post-action failure together, so the run ends after that action's `tool_finished`. (4) The omission notice carries `warning: "workspace_capture_incomplete"` beside the report, so the model and a test can tell it from a failure. (5) The ten integration pins that asserted the broker rethrows the store's raw `private_agent_unresolved_dispatch` now assert the typed `BrokerError("unresolved_dispatch")`; the two direct `store.commit` pins are unchanged. (6) The host notice after a capture failure or an omission report is a user message generated from the recorded fields, live and on replay, as the design entry's refinement of A records; `tool_finished.output` is never overwritten by a later capture failure.

Changes: src/main/private-agent/sandbox.ts: `SANDBOX_ERROR_CODES`; the sorted, reporting lister (`LIST_FILES`, exported for the host-side test) with sizes, the fixed reasons `symlink`, `hard_link`, `special`, `oversize`, `name_invalid` (counted, never named) and `cap`, the 4,096-entry stop with `complete: false`, and die() only for the walk's own failure; `parseWorkspaceListing`, `WorkspaceListing`, `WORKSPACE_OMISSION_REASONS`, `WORKSPACE_LISTING_MAX_ENTRIES` (4,096), `WORKSPACE_LISTING_MAX_OMITTED_PATHS` (32); `boundedOutputCollector` and the `truncate` option that `execute` alone sets, with the fixed `[host]` overflow note appended to stderr. runner.ts: `captureCheckpoint` (never throws; a fixed code plus the original error) and `capture` (omits beyond 128 MiB with `total_cap`); the capture-failure handling at the action, pre-stop, finish and allowance captures, `captureFailure`, `recheckCaptureFailure` and `captureOmitted` on `tool_finished`, `captureFailure` on `host_validation_finished`, the container recreation from the last checkpoint, the per-run failure counter, `captureNotice` on the live path and on replay; the broker-denial branch (`broker_denied` marker, the size stop from `details`, the outcomes `cancelled_or_deadline` or paused, `packet_scan_unavailable`, `model_request_denied`, `unresolved_dispatch_no_replay`) and the resume checks that accept the marker and end a recurring refusal again; `toolFailureFeedback` over the fixed table; `brokerCode` on `runtime_failure`. tool-errors.ts (new): `ToolError`, `GENERIC_TOOL_FAILURE`, `TOOL_ERROR_FEEDBACK`, the code enums. observations.ts: `validateFailure` accepts the sandbox objects for an unavailable execute, the read refusals for a refused read, and `execution_context_unavailable` for either not-invoked tool, byte for byte; the two read errors are `ToolError`s. model.ts: `BROKER_DENIED_STOP`, `BROKER_DENIAL_CODES` (six codes), `PACKET_SCAN_UNAVAILABLE_STOP`, `MODEL_REQUEST_DENIED_STOP`, `modelRequestBrokerDenied`, the join in `hasInvalidModelRequestSizeStop`. broker.ts: `BrokerError.details`, `packet_size_exceeded` with its numbers for a body over the cap, the store's unresolved refusal wrapped as `unresolved_dispatch`. general-tasks/controller.ts: the two fixed reasons, their status mapping, `canResume` for `packet_scan_unavailable`, `uncertain()` accepting the marker, the event summary. Tests: tests/unit/private-agent-sandbox-capture.test.ts (new: the lister script under the machine's python3 on a temporary directory; the parser's refusals; the collector), tests/helpers/workspace-listing.ts (new), tests/unit/private-agent-runner-budget.test.ts (the pre-stop test rewritten from refusing replay to running the action; the post-action, double, finish and allowance capture failures; the omission report; `execution_context_unavailable`; each broker denial code and the real-broker ledger refusal; `brokerCode`; the sandbox codes and the host codes as fixed objects; the fixture's lister shape and path rule), private-agent-observations.test.ts, private-agent-model-size.test.ts, private-agent-public-research.test.ts (`destination_denied`), general-task-controller.test.ts (the two reasons and a malformed marker), the four other fixtures that mock `listFiles`, tests/integration/private-agent-broker.test.ts and private-agent-consultant.test.ts (the typed code), tests/integration/private-agent-sandbox.test.ts (links omitted with the container usable; bounded output with the container usable and the cut marked; the listing shape).

Evidence: At this entry's commit, `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3`: 165 files, 152 passed and 13 skipped (the environment-gated Docker, model and end-to-end suites, as before), 2479 tests passed and 81 skipped; PR #38's head had 2450 passed with the same skips. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm validate:readiness` and `pnpm --silent validate:build-log -- --base-ref origin/fix/assist-purpose-exception` pass; tests/unit/private-agent-identity-golden.test.ts passes untouched, so `promptProtocolSha256` (76f77ad3...) and the identity pin did not move and every paused task resumes under its recorded identity. The deterministic tests prove, on fixtures: a failed post-action capture records `tool_finished` with `captureFailure` and the observation module's own output, a checkpoint carrying the prior snapshot, no `runtime_failure`, a container recreated from that checkpoint and a user notice right after the tool result, and the run completes; two consecutive failures end `runtime_failure_progress_preserved` with the original sandbox code, both operations closed, and a reopened run completes; a failed pre-stop recheck runs the warned action against the recreated checkpoint, records `recheckCaptureFailure` and never a `model_action_not_started`, and a failed recreation before the action answers `execution_context_unavailable` and recreates again; a failed finish capture answers without verifying and a later finish completes; a failed allowance capture closes the validation and a later run finds `host_validation_not_replayed`; an omission report reaches the event and the model; the lister script run under python3 omits a symlink, a hard link, a FIFO, a sparse oversize file and two refused names with the fixed reasons and counts, never follows a directory link, keeps the first 1,024 files and stops at 4,096 entries with an incomplete report, and dies only when the walk itself fails; the parser refuses every malformed shape as `unsafe_file`; the collector fails closed for protocol calls and keeps exactly the cap for execute; each of the six broker codes records its marker and outcome with nothing dispatched, the size numbers record the size stop, a recurring refusal ends every later run, a cancel pauses or ends cancelled and the next run completes, a scanner failure resumes, the ledger's refusal reaches the runner typed through the real broker, and `transport_or_settlement_unknown` still ends without resume with `brokerCode` recorded; a denied fetch destination sends nothing; the controller maps `packet_scan_unavailable` resumable, `model_request_denied` not, and a malformed marker as uncertain.

Failures or blockers: None in the deterministic suites. CI has not run on this branch yet (it runs on the pull request). The Docker-gated suites skipped here, so the three rewritten integration cases (omitted links with a usable container, bounded output with a usable container, the listing shape) have not run.

The lister's behaviour inside the container, the exec truncation through the Docker client and the `[host]` overflow note were not exercised against Docker; the lister ran under the host's python3 on a temporary directory, and the collector was tested as a unit. Pre-commit policy refusals outside the six codes and a failed verifier at allowance exhaustion keep today's outcome. ### BL-20261107-1006-stop-bricking-tasks-review-corrections -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 3, review corrections decided: every pre-context failure answers execution_context_unavailable, the path rule refuses a non-UTF-8 name instead of dying, cloud_after_assist_unknown is the seventh denial code, a missing destination at the deadline guard ends model_request_denied, a finish whose verifier failed answers verification_unavailable, and the error table is pinned

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: The decision entry for the corrections that an adversarial three-lens review (invariants, privacy and persisted contracts, dispatch semantics; each lens read `git diff 6f735fa..bc03d75` read-only) found in backlog item 3's implementation (BL-20261107-0936-stop-bricking-tasks-implemented), recorded before their code because two of them widen persisted contracts: the `broker_denied` marker's code enum and the fixed tool-error table that the observation verifier accepts byte for byte. The lenses returned "mergeable with fixes" with one finding in common, found independently by all three: a plain error thrown while the container is recreated before an action records the generic failure object on a not-invoked execute, which the verifier is now defined to reject, so one transient checkpoint-store fault bricks the task permanently, the class of defect item 3 exists to remove. Hypothesis: with the nine decisions below no path added by item 3 can record a `tool_finished` the verifier rejects, the lister's decision B holds for every name, the pre-commit refusals the runner can meet from its own model request are the seven named codes, and every fixed text the model receives after a failure is true of the state the host left. Zero-fee code with deterministic tests; no approval is needed under PLAN.md section 4, so the implementation follows in the same pull request.

Decisions: (1, all three lenses) Before the action's container is ready, every failure answers `execution_context_unavailable`: `toolFailureFeedback` returns that object for any error class while `contextReady` is false, not only for a `SandboxError`, because the only code that runs before the flag is set is the recreation itself (`checkpoints.load` and `DockerSandbox.create`), so nothing was invoked by construction. Without this, `checkpoints.load`'s plain errors (`checkpoint_file_invalid`, `checkpoint_digest_mismatch`, a missing file) recorded the generic object with `executionCapture: "not_invoked"`, the acceptance set for that case is exactly `execution_context_unavailable`, and every later projection and resume threw `ObservationIntegrityError`. (2, privacy lens) The protocol scripts' shared path rule `valid()` returns False for a name that is not valid UTF-8 (Python's scandir yields such a name surrogate-escaped and `str.encode('utf-8')` then raises `UnicodeEncodeError`, which reached the lister's `die()`), so the lister counts it `name_invalid` as decision B of BL-20261107-0924 states, and the read, edit and import protocols, which call `if not valid(p): die()`, keep failing closed. A host-side unit case creates such a name where the filesystem admits one (Linux, where CI runs `pnpm check`) and is skipped where it refuses one (APFS); a Docker-gated case creates it inside the container. (3, invariants and semantics lenses) `cloud_after_assist_unknown` becomes the seventh code of `BROKER_DENIAL_CODES`, outcome `model_request_denied`, listed among the refusals that recur: the broker denies it inside the commit callback before any row exists whenever a grant-free cloud dispatch follows an assist row that stayed `unknown`, and nothing resolves such a row today, so a later run ends the same way without a request. It is reachable from the runner's own model request once a cloud execution destination follows an unknown assist of another context (item 10's exemption lets the loop proceed past that row), latent until item 13 issues an assist, and as pre-commit and deterministic as a blocked scan; left out, it rethrew with an open `model_started` and every later run ended `unresolved_operation_no_replay`. The enum widens before any marker was recorded (the item is unreleased). (4, semantics lens) A `destination_missing` raised by the deadline guard (`model.deadlineRefuses` calls `broker.requestTimeoutMs`), which runs before `model_started`, ends the run `model_request_denied` directly, with no marker because nothing is open; this is the production path for a missing destination, so the decided outcome and its fixed desktop text now hold, and the handled branch keeps the same mapping as a second site. (5, invariants lens) A `finish` whose capture succeeded but whose container close or verifier failed answers the new fixed object `verification_unavailable` (the eleventh host code): the workspace is retained as the latest checkpoint, verification did not run, call finish again. The sandbox objects it returned before say the workspace was recreated from the last checkpoint and later changes are lost, which is false for this path: the snapshot had already advanced to the finish capture. (6, privacy lens) `sandbox_unusable` no longer claims `actionInvoked: false`: the code is also thrown after a protocol call returned when the container had become unusable during it, so the host cannot prove nothing ran; its text now says the host cannot tell. (7, privacy lens) The retry loop's top-of-attempt cancel check raises `retry_wait_cancelled` instead of `request_cancelled`: at that site (attempt > 1) an earlier attempt was sent and resolved `superseded`, so the request was dispatched, and the runner already maps that code to `model_request_failed` with `dispatched: true` and the cancelled or paused outcome. No await separates the site from the post-backoff abort check, so no test can reach it; the change is for truthfulness. (8, invariants lens) A golden test pins the tool-error table (a digest of the whole table and of the generic object) and the three capture-notice objects exactly: the verifier accepts the table byte for byte and the notice is regenerated on replay, neither is bound into the prompt protocol by design (binding would end every paused task in `runtime_contract_drift`), so a text change must be a deliberate, logged decision. (9) Not changed, with the reasoning recorded: `job_cancelled` cannot be raised for the model request, because the controller aborts the signal before it cancels the policy and no await separates the broker's post-scan signal check from `store.commit`, inside which `eligible()` runs (a local admission cancel surfaces as the admission error, already handled); the other pre-commit eligibility refusals (`exact_grant_required`, `cloud_mode_denied`, `offline_network_denied`, `credential_context_denied`, `public_dns_requires_public_context`, `synthetic_destination_private_data_denied`, `assist_destination_invalid`, the local-model admission rules) are configuration refusals the desktop's local route cannot raise today; on a misconfigured cloud route they would leave a `model_started` open, and they are deferred to item 13, named here so the Implemented entry's hypothesis reads as "the seven named refusals". `path_invalid` stays the mapping for an edit tool's `invalid_input` because the argument schemas (content of at most 32,768 UTF-16 units, so at most 98,304 bytes; a non-empty `old`; a combined replace of at most 196,608 bytes) keep every model edit under the sandbox's size rules, so the path rule is the only `invalid_input` an edit can hit; a code comment records the arithmetic.

Changes: Planned in this pull request on branch `fix/stop-bricking-tasks`: runner.ts (`toolFailureFeedback`'s context check first; `DENIED_WITHOUT_RESUME` gains the seventh code; the deadline guard's `destination_missing` catch; the finish branch's `verification_unavailable` wrap; `captureNotice` exported for the pin; the `path_invalid` comment), sandbox.ts (`valid()` with the `UnicodeEncodeError` guard), model.ts (the seventh code and its comment), tool-errors.ts (`verification_unavailable`; `sandbox_unusable` without `actionInvoked`), broker.ts (`retry_wait_cancelled` at the top-of-attempt check). Tests: tests/unit/private-agent-runner-budget.test.ts (a plain checkpoint-store error during the recreation answers `execution_context_unavailable` and the run completes; `cloud_after_assist_unknown` in the recurring-refusal cases; `destination_missing` from the deadline guard with no marker and no `model_started`; a finish whose verifier failed answers `verification_unavailable`, keeps the finish snapshot and completes on the next finish), tests/unit/private-agent-sandbox-capture.test.ts (the non-UTF-8 name, skipped where the filesystem refuses it), tests/integration/private-agent-sandbox.test.ts (the non-UTF-8 name inside the container), tests/unit/private-agent-model-size.test.ts and tests/unit/general-task-controller.test.ts (the seventh code), tests/unit/private-agent-tool-errors-golden.test.ts (new).

Evidence: The review's findings, each with the sites it cited, re-read at bc03d75 by the recording session: (1) runner.ts sets `executionCapture = "not_invoked"` and then evaluates `checkpoints.load(snapshot)` inside the action try; checkpoints.ts throws plain `Error`s there; `toolFailureFeedback` gates `execution_context_unavailable` on `error instanceof SandboxError`; observations.ts accepts only that object for a not-invoked execute and tests/unit/private-agent-observations.test.ts pins that the generic is rejected there. (2) `valid()` computes `len(p.encode('utf-8'))` with no handler; the lister's `except BaseException: die()` catches the raise. (3) broker.ts denies `cloud_after_assist_unknown` inside the commit callback; `BROKER_DENIAL_CODES` lists six codes; the runner's branch rethrows any other `BrokerError` with `model_started` recorded and no marker. (4) `deadlineRefuses` runs before `model_started` and `requestTimeoutMs` denies `destination_missing`; the existing test injects the code through the model mock, so it proved the branch, not the production path. (5) the finish branch closes the frozen container and verifies after the capture succeeded, inside the same try, and `toolFailureFeedback` with `contextReady` true maps a failure there to a `sandbox_*` object whose text names the recreation. (6) sandbox.ts throws `unusable` both before the call and after it returned. (7) broker.ts checks `attempt > 1 && signal.aborted` only after a `superseded` resolution and `continue`. (8) tool-errors.ts and `captureNotice` are deliberately outside `promptProtocol`. Severities as returned: invariants two major and three minor; privacy one blocker, one major and two minor; semantics one major and three minor. Each lens also listed what it confirmed sound (every new path closes its operation; checkpoint order; the marker join; the privacy of every new persisted field; the protocol pin untouched), which this entry does not restate.

Failures or blockers: None in recording. The review lenses were read-only and ran no suite; their severity labels are theirs, the decisions above are this session's.

Limitations and non-claims: This entry decides; nothing is implemented or verified by it. Decision (2)'s host-side case cannot run on APFS, which refuses a non-UTF-8 name; its proof on this Mac is the Docker-gated case, recorded in a later `Verified` entry, and its proof in CI is the Linux runner. Decision (7) changes a branch no test can reach. Decision (9) leaves the other pre-commit refusals as they are. Nothing here touches a live model, a paid destination or product quality.
