### BL-20261107-1041-stop-bricking-tasks-second-review-corrections -- 2026-11-07 -- Backlog item 3, second review corrections decided: no capture on a container the action's own failure destroyed, a recheck notice that is true when nothing ran, a finished validation for every allowance-path failure, and three wording fixes

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: The decision entry for what a second adversarial three-lens review (runtime invariants, persisted contracts and replay, completeness against the first review) found in the uncommitted implementation of BL-20261107-1006-stop-bricking-tasks-review-corrections, recorded before the code because one decision adds a persisted field (`host_validation_finished.verificationFailure`) and two change the bytes of host texts the model receives. The lenses confirmed all nine decisions of BL-20261107-1006 delivered and found three things beside them, two of which all three lenses raised independently. Hypothesis: with the four decisions below, every fixed text the model receives after a failure is true of the state the host left (the hypothesis BL-20261107-1006 stated and, on two paths, did not meet), an action the sandbox refused or lost never counts as a workspace capture failure, and no path item 3 touched leaves a `host_validation_started` unmatched. Zero-fee code with deterministic tests; no approval is needed under PLAN.md section 4, so the implementation follows in the same pull request.

Decisions: (10, all three lenses) No capture is attempted on a container the action's own failure destroyed. `DockerSandbox.operation()` closes the container on every error raised inside a call (`unavailable`, `command_timeout`, `cancelled`, `output_limit`, `unsafe_file`, the post-call `unusable`), and refuses `unusable` before a call on a container already closed; only `invalid_input` and `busy` leave it intact. The runner nevertheless captured on that object after recording the action's fixed result, so the capture failed `unusable` by construction, the model was told in the next message that the action ran and the workspace was recreated (while the result had just said the host cannot tell whether it ran), and the foredoomed capture counted toward the two-consecutive-failures stop, so two actions the sandbox lost in a row (two writes through a symlinked path part, two daemon failures) ended the run `runtime_failure_progress_preserved` with `sandbox_unusable`. Now the action catch drops the container reference for every `SandboxError` but `invalid_input` and `busy`: no capture, no `captureFailure`, no notice, no counter increment; the checkpoint recorded with the result carries the prior snapshot as before, and the recreation that follows the result rebuilds the container from it, which the sandbox object's own text already says. The capture-failure counter therefore counts only captures of a live container. The unit fixture's mock sandbox hid this because it never became unusable after a thrown error; it now does, as `operation()` does, so the suite exercises the production sequence. (11, invariants lens) The recheck notice has two forms, both pure functions of the recorded event: when `executionCapture` is `not_invoked` (the recreation before the warned action failed, or its arguments were invalid), it says the host could not capture the workspace to check it, recreates it from the last checkpoint so background changes since then are not retained, and that this action did not run, as its result says; otherwise it keeps the text that says the action ran against the recreated workspace. The single text asserted the recreation and the run on the exact path decision (1) of BL-20261107-1006 fixed, where both were false. (12, invariants lens; pre-existing at the branch base and kept by BL-20261107-0936 as a non-claim) On the allowance path, after the capture's checkpoint is recorded, the container close, the cancel-or-deadline check and the verifier run inside one handler: a failure or an abort there records `host_validation_finished` with `passed: false`, `checks: []`, the missing artifacts and a new `verificationFailure: { code }`, where `code` is `sandbox_<code>` for a `SandboxError`, `cancelled_or_deadline` for the abort, or `verification_failed` for anything else, and the run ends `cancelled_or_deadline` or `bounded_allowance_exhausted`; a later run finds a finished validation (`host_validation_not_replayed`) instead of ending `unresolved_operation_no_replay` with the desktop showing an uncertain outcome for a path where nothing was sent and the checkpoint is durable. The field is additive: selection.ts compares `verifiedSnapshotSha256` against the final snapshot and treats its absence as not current, and the controller's submission issues count a failed validation as before. The existing test that pinned the no-replay stop is rewritten to the finished validation. (13, three minor findings) The `verification_unavailable` text names both causes it covers ("the container could not be released, or the verifier could not be started, failed or was stopped"); the desktop's fixed `model_request_denied` text names the ledger rule beside the destination and packet rules, since the seventh code is neither; the broker's in-callback cancel check denies `retry_wait_cancelled` on a retry attempt, like the top-of-attempt check decision (7) changed, both guards no test can reach. Recorded, not changed: the ordinal "eleventh host code" in BL-20261107-1006 and "tenth" in BL-20261107-0936 count the generic object and the fetch-failure object beside the enum; `verification_unavailable` is the ninth entry of `HOST_TOOL_ERROR_CODES` and `execution_context_unavailable` was the eighth. Decision (9)'s list of deferred pre-commit refusals also includes `private_disclosure_requires_exact_grant`, which the desktop's local route cannot raise either.

Changes: Planned in this pull request on branch `fix/stop-bricking-tasks`: runner.ts (the action catch drops the destroyed container; `captureNotice`'s two recheck forms; the allowance path's handler and `verificationFailure`), tool-errors.ts and general-tasks/controller.ts (the two texts), broker.ts (the in-callback cancel code). Tests: tests/unit/private-agent-runner-budget.test.ts (the fixture's mock sandbox becomes unusable after a closing error and gains a close hook; the sandbox-code case asserts no `captureFailure` and no notice; two consecutive lost actions continue and complete; the notice after a failed recreation says nothing ran; the allowance verifier that cannot start, a close that fails and a deadline after the checkpoint each record a finished validation that a later run finds), tests/unit/private-agent-tool-errors-golden.test.ts (the second recheck form; the moved table digest).

Evidence: The second review's findings, re-read at the working tree by the recording session: (10) runner.ts drops no reference in the action catch and captures on `sandbox` for every action; sandbox.ts `operation()` closes on every in-call error and refuses `unusable` before a call; the notice's capture-failure object asserts `actionInvoked: true`; the fixture's mock `execute` throws without flipping any flag and its `listFiles` keeps answering, so the sandbox-code test saw no `captureFailure`. (11) `captureNotice` emits one recheck text whatever `executionCapture` says; the decision (1) test asserts the event and the result but not the notice. (12) the allowance path's `sandbox.close()` is unwrapped, the abort check returns before `host_validation_finished`, and `this.verify()`'s throw reaches the outer catch, all three leaving `host_validation_started` open; identical lines exist at the branch base 6f735fa. (13) the three texts and the callback site as cited. The lenses' confirmed-sound lists (every decision of BL-20261107-1006 delivered at its site; the enum widening's readers; the verifier's acceptance sets built from the live table; the lister's Python semantics; the golden pins reproduced from the working tree) are not restated here. They also noted that decision (6) of BL-20261107-1006 changed the bytes of an object the verifier accepts (`sandbox_unusable`), which this entry's Implemented successor states explicitly.

Failures or blockers: None in recording. The review lenses were read-only and ran no suite.

Limitations and non-claims: This entry decides; nothing is implemented or verified by it. Decision (10) does not change what the model is told for a lost action (the sandbox object), only removes the false notice and the miscounted failure. Decision (12) does not make an exhausted allowance resumable; it corrects the recorded outcome and the desktop's label. The lister's remaining `die()` for an entry that vanishes or changes type between its scandir and its stat is decision B's reserved case, unchanged. Nothing here touches a live model, a paid destination or product quality.

Paid exposure: None. Zero SOAR model requests and zero envelope spend.

Status: `Implemented`

Scope or hypothesis: Implement BL-20261107-1006-stop-bricking-tasks-review-corrections (decisions 1 to 9) and BL-20261107-1041-stop-bricking-tasks-second-review-corrections (decisions 10 to 13) as decided, with deterministic tests, on branch `fix/stop-bricking-tasks` (based on `fix/assist-purpose-exception`, PR #38, itself on PR #37). Decisions: None new beyond the two decision entries. Statements of fact for the record: (a) decision (6) of BL-20261107-1006 changed the bytes of an object the observation verifier accepts byte for byte (`sandbox_unusable`: the instruction replaced, `actionInvoked: false` removed), so a `tool_finished` recorded by the first implementation (bc03d75) with the old object for an execute the sandbox lost would now be rejected on resume; no such event exists, because that code never ran against a real task and the item is unreleased, and the golden pin now guards the bytes. The texts of `verification_unavailable` and of the recheck notice likewise moved within this pull request, before any release. (b) `verification_unavailable` is the ninth entry of `HOST_TOOL_ERROR_CODES` and `execution_context_unavailable` was the eighth; the ordinals "eleventh" (BL-20261107-1006) and "tenth" (BL-20261107-0936) counted the generic object and the fetch-failure object beside the enum. The table holds eighteen objects, nine host codes and nine sandbox codes. (c) The pre-commit refusals decision (9) defers to item 13 also include `private_disclosure_requires_exact_grant`, which the desktop's local route cannot raise either. (d) Decision (10)'s list of in-call codes also includes `cleanup_failed`, which `operation()` surfaces when its own destroying close throws; the drop in the action catch covers it. (e) For the allowance path's cancel-or-deadline variant of decision (12), a later run ends `cancelled_or_deadline` while the cancel or the contract deadline persists, because that check precedes the finished-validation check; `host_validation_not_replayed` is the outcome of the verifier and close variants. Neither ends `unresolved_operation_no_replay`, which is the point. Details fixed in code, each proposed by the focused review of the second round: (1) `toolFailureFeedback` tests `contextReady` before every other classification, so the order itself is the proof that nothing thrown before the flag is set is treated as an argument error or a host refusal; (2) decision (11)'s kept recheck form says the action was started against the recreated workspace and that its result says how it ended, since a lost container leaves the run itself unknown; (3) the desktop's fixed summary for a `host_validation_finished` the host closed without a verifier result (a capture failure or a `verificationFailure`) says the frozen artifact could not be verified and the validation is closed, instead of "Structural checks recorded."; (4) `VerificationFailureCode` closes the recorded code set at the type level, like `CaptureFailureCode`; (5) the deadline-guard test drives the real chain (a model whose destination the fixture's broker lacks, so `requestTimeoutMs` itself refuses), and the sandbox-code tests pin the keep half of decision (10) by container-create counts.

### BL-20261108-0904-owner-verdict-capture-design -- 2026-11-08 -- Decide backlog item 2, owner verdict capture: a verdict field on the desktop task record, a verdict receipt, and registry verdict rows through registry-row.py

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: Review section 5.7 item 2 (docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md; S12 in section 5.2; one OAJ row per owner job in section 5.9): the owner records accept or reject, minutes and interventions on a submitted desktop task, and that verdict reaches docs/experiments/registry.jsonl through scripts/registry-row.py, which today rows only a headless run directory or an H4 loop. Two persisted contracts change, so this decision entry precedes the code. Everything below is proposed for the owner to confirm or override; nothing is implemented by this entry.

Decisions: (1) Registry verdict rows. scripts/registry-row.py gains a `--supersedes ROW_ID` mode with `--registry PATH` (default: the repository's docs/experiments/registry.jsonl). It loads the registry, finds the row with that id, refuses an unknown id, an id another row already supersedes, and a new id that already exists, copies the row verbatim (every measurement, `taskJobSha256`, `date`, `usd`, `entailment`, `loop`) and sets only the new `id`, `supersedes`, `outcome`, `verdictBy`, `ownerMinutes`, `interventions`, `lesson` and a new optional `verdictAt` (UTC ISO 8601 from `--verdict-at`, default the writing time). `batch`, `task`, `family`, `exposure` and `arm` are copied unless re-declared and stay required for every other row; `git` stays `git rev-parse HEAD` at writing time, today's behaviour (finding E4 belongs to item 11); `date` stays the run's date. (2) A third exclusive source, `--verdict-file RECEIPT.json`, rows a desktop task from the app's verdict receipt (decision 4). Exactly one of `--run-dir`, `--loop-dir`, `--verdict-file` and `--supersedes` is accepted. The receipt fills `taskJobSha256`, `date`, `profile`, `thinking`, `maxOutputTokens`, `runStatus`, `terminalCause`, `modelCalls`, `toolCalls`, `wallSeconds`, the five token and length-stop counts, `usd`, the three dispatch counts, `entailment`, `arm`, `cloudModel: null`, `cloudApi: null`, `outcome` (accept to `accepted`, reject to `rejected`), `ownerMinutes`, `interventions`, `verdictAt` and a new optional boolean `exportedThroughApp` (an OAJ condition, PLAN.md section 1); the operator types `--id`, `--batch`, `--task`, `--family`, `--exposure`, `--lesson` and `--verdict-by owner`, so no free text typed in the app reaches the public registry; `--outcome`, `--owner-minutes`, `--interventions`, `--verdict-at` and `--arm` may be repeated but must match the receipt. The CLI refuses a receipt with an unknown key, a wrong `version` or a missing `verdict`. (3) `verdictBy` is validated against the README enum `owner`, `agent_diagnostic`, `none` for every row the script writes; the registry's historical values (`host_gate`, `qualified_checker`, `qualified_checker+agent_screenshot_review`, `agent_diagnostic_blind` and free-text strings naming the checking model) are documented as legacy and never re-rowed. `--verdict-by owner` requires `--owner-minutes` (finite, at least 0) and an explicit `--interventions` (integer, at least 0); other rows keep `ownerMinutes: null`, `interventions: 0` and refuse `--owner-minutes`. (4) Desktop record. The persisted `TaskRecord` in src/main/general-tasks/controller.ts gains an optional `verdict` field (`decision` accept or reject, `ownerMinutes`, `interventions`, `exportedThroughApp`, `recordedAt`), validated when present, with no version bump (older records lack it). `recordVerdict` parses a strict zod schema `GeneralTaskVerdictInputSchema` (`id`, `decision`, `ownerMinutes` finite 0 to 600, `interventions` integer 0 to 99, `exportedThroughApp`; no free-text field), accepts only a `submitted` task with no active session (`general_task_verdict_denied`), refuses a second verdict (`general_task_verdict_recorded`; a correction is a registry `supersedes` row at the CLI), saves without moving `updatedAt` (the version 3 elapsed-time projection reads it as the finish time), publishes, and the snapshot gains an optional `verdict`. `independentAcceptance` stays `not_evaluated` and `reportedIssues` are untouched: an owner verdict is the OAJ mark, not independent acceptance. (5) `verdictReceipt(id)` returns canonical JSON with an allow-listed key set only: `version: 1`, `taskId`, `taskJobSha256` (the record's attestation identity, precedent BL-20261012-1625-owner-job-classified), `date` (UTC date of `startedAt`), `profile`, `thinking`, `maxOutputTokens`, `runStatus`, `terminalCause`, `modelCalls`, `toolCalls`, `wallSeconds` (the task time the app shows), `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cachedTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens` and `lengthStops` summed from `model_finished` events as registry-row.py does (the entailment pass writes no model events, so it stays excluded as the README requires), `usd` (settled fees), `unknownDispatches`, `retriedDispatches`, `failedDispatches`, `entailment` (counts, calls, truncated, support rate, or null), `arm` (`local-<profile>`, or `local-<profile>-consulted` when a consultation settled), `verdict` with `recordedAt` as UTC ISO 8601, `cloudModel: null`, `cloudApi: null`. Never the goal, file names, paths, URLs or model text. (6) Two IPC channels, `soar:general-task-record-verdict` and `soar:general-task-export-verdict-receipt`, with the sender assertions and the native save-dialog pattern of the existing export handlers; preload methods `recordGeneralTaskVerdict` and `exportGeneralTaskVerdictReceipt`; an "Owner verdict" section in the general-task workspace shown only for a submitted task when the bridge exposes `recordGeneralTaskVerdict` (feature-checked like `exportGeneralTaskBundle`, not added to the `hasApi` list, so older preloads keep the workspace). (7) Rejected: a `--desktop-db` mode that opens the app's database. The live SQLite is shared with the running app, the script's event query has no job filter, and the `general_tasks` row holds the goal text. (8) Rejected: overwriting a verdict in the app, or a verdict on an `incomplete` or `cancelled` task; PLAN.md section 1 counts OAJ over submitted jobs.

Changes: This entry only. The implementation, its tests, the docs/experiments/README.md row documentation and the `Implemented` entry follow in the same pull request once the deterministic tests pass. No registry row, configuration or earlier entry changes.

Evidence: Reading only, at commit 456344e: scripts/registry-row.py (two sources, `--verdict-by` unvalidated, `--interventions` defaulting to 0, `git` at writing time), the registry's 99 rows (one `verdictBy: owner` row, `oaj-20261012-document-review-1`, hand-written from UI metadata with null token counts and `ownerMinutes: null`; five hand-written superseding rows; six distinct non-enum `verdictBy` values), src/main/general-tasks/controller.ts (`TaskRecord`, `record()`, `save()`, `get()`, the `submitted` projection), src/main/general-tasks-ipc.ts (the export handlers' sender re-check and temporary-file save), src/main/private-agent/runner.ts (`model_finished` carries `usage` and `finishReason`), src/main/private-agent/session.ts (the entailment pass calls the model directly and writes only `claims_entailment`), docs/experiments/README.md and docs/PLAN.md section 1 (OAJ) and section 4 (one registry row per run with owner verdict, owner minutes and interventions).

Failures or blockers: None. Open for the owner: whether `git` on a superseding row should instead keep the original run's commit, as the five hand-written superseding rows did; whether `exportedThroughApp` belongs in the row (decision 2) or only in the receipt; and the batch and task-id convention for E5's owner rows (the precedent uses batch `owner-real-jobs` and task `owner-<first 8 hex of the task id>`), which E5's card fixes before the first owner job is rowed.

Limitations and non-claims: Proposed only. Nothing here is implemented, tested or verified, and no owner job is rowed by this entry. The receipt binds hashes and counts, not the deliverable's quality; a verdict row is the owner's judgement, recorded beside the three columns, and supplies no independent acceptance. The receipt's token counts cover the local writer's model events only; a consultation's tokens are not in the token columns, its settled fee is in `usd`.

Paid exposure: None. Zero SOAR model requests and zero envelope spend.

Next gate: The owner confirms or overrides decisions 1 to 8; the implementation lands with deterministic tests and its `Implemented` entry; the first owner verdict is rowed only after E5's experiment card is committed (docs/HANDOFF.md, "Start here", step 4).

### BL-20261108-0905-owner-verdict-capture-implemented -- 2026-11-08 -- Implement backlog item 2, owner verdict capture: desktop verdict record and receipt, two IPC channels, the workspace section, and registry-row.py's --verdict-file and --supersedes modes

Status: `Implemented`

Scope or hypothesis: Implement BL-20261108-0904-owner-verdict-capture-design (docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.7 item 2, S12 in section 5.2) as proposed there: the optional `verdict` on the desktop task record, the hashes-and-counts verdict receipt, the two IPC channels and preload methods, the "Owner verdict" section of the general-task workspace, and scripts/registry-row.py's `--verdict-file` and `--supersedes` modes, with deterministic offline tests. Implemented is not Verified: no owner job has been rowed and no owner has used the section.

Decisions: The design entry's decisions 1 to 8 are implemented as written, with these implementation choices. (a) `recordVerdict` saves the record without moving `updatedAt` (`save(record, { touch: false })`), because the version 3 elapsed-time projection reads `updatedAt` as the finish time; the revision still increments so the renderer accepts the new snapshot. (b) The receipt is canonical JSON (sorted keys, one trailing newline) over the exported `VERDICT_RECEIPT_KEYS` list, which the controller test compares key for key and which the Python writer mirrors as `RECEIPT_KEYS`; the receipt's `recordedAt` keeps milliseconds and the row's `verdictAt` is normalised to whole seconds in the `Z` form. (c) In `--verdict-file` mode `--outcome`, `--owner-minutes`, `--interventions`, `--verdict-at` and `--arm` are optional and, when given, must equal the receipt's values; `--arm` is optional in that mode because the receipt names it. (d) In `--supersedes` mode the new `id` must not already exist, a duplicated original id is refused as ambiguous, `criticalChecks` is kept unless re-declared, and a non-owner superseding row keeps `ownerMinutes: null` and `interventions: 0`. (e) The receipt validator accepts only identifiers (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`) for `profile`, `thinking`, `runStatus` and `terminalCause`, `local-(standard|heavy)(-consulted)?` for `arm`, a UUID for `taskId`, a SHA-256 digest for `taskJobSha256`, counts, non-negative amounts, `null` cloud fields and exactly the documented `verdict` and `entailment` keys. (f) The verdict form has no text field: two radios, two number inputs and one checkbox, validated through the shared zod schema before the call, and the section is feature-checked on `recordGeneralTaskVerdict` rather than added to `hasApi`.

Changes: src/shared/general-task-contracts.ts (`GeneralTaskVerdictInputSchema`, `GeneralTaskVerdictSchema`, optional `verdict` on the snapshot, `recordGeneralTaskVerdict` and `exportGeneralTaskVerdictReceipt`, two channels); src/main/general-tasks/controller.ts (optional `verdict` on `TaskRecord`, validated in `record()`; the `save` touch option; the projection; `recordVerdict`; `verdictReceipt`; `VERDICT_RECEIPT_KEYS`); src/main/general-tasks-ipc.ts (the two handlers, same sender assertions and temporary-file save as the exports); src/preload/index.ts (two methods); src/renderer/src/GeneralTaskWorkspace.tsx and general-task.css (the "Owner verdict" section); scripts/registry-row.py (`--verdict-file`, `--supersedes`, `--registry`, `--verdict-at`, the `verdictBy` enum, the owner-effort rule; the H4 loop block is unchanged in place); docs/experiments/README.md (`verdictBy` legacy values, `verdictAt`, `supersedes`, `exportedThroughApp`, the owner-verdict-rows section, the finding E11 exclusion rule). Tests: tests/unit/registry-row-verdict.test.ts and tests/unit/preload-general-task-api.test.ts are new; tests/unit/general-task-controller.test.ts, general-task-consultation-controller.test.ts, general-task-ipc.test.ts, app-general-task.test.tsx and registry-row-loop.test.ts gain cases. No registry row, configuration, end-to-end spec or earlier entry changes.

Evidence: On this working tree with Node 22.22.2, pnpm 10.12.4 and the machine's Python 3.9: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm validate:readiness` pass; `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/registry-row-loop.test.ts tests/unit/registry-row-verdict.test.ts tests/unit/preload-general-task-api.test.ts` 8 of 8; `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/general-task-controller.test.ts tests/unit/general-task-consultation-controller.test.ts` 114 of 114; `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/general-task-ipc.test.ts tests/unit/app-general-task.test.tsx` 76 of 76; `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3`: 152 files passed and 13 environment-gated files skipped, 2439 tests passed and 81 skipped, 85 s, exit 0 (run before a documentation-only fix to the README's shell example, which no test reads). The deterministic tests prove: the writer's `--supersedes` mode copies every field but the verdict fields, `supersedes`, `verdictAt` and `git`, and refuses an unknown, already superseded or reused id; `--verdict-file` emits the documented row from a receipt and refuses unknown keys (`goal`, `path`, `url`, `outputName`), a wrong version, a missing or malformed verdict, non-identifier text and a cloud model; the exactly-one-of-four source rule across every pair; the owner-effort rule and the `verdictBy` enum; the controller records one verdict on a submitted inactive task only, refuses queued, running, paused, incomplete and cancelled tasks and a second verdict, persists it across reopening, refuses a tampered record, leaves `independentAcceptance`, `reportedIssues`, `updatedAt` and `elapsedMs` unchanged, and publishes once; the receipt has exactly the allow-listed keys, `taskJobSha256` equals the record's attestation identity, its counts match the fixture's events and dispatches, its text contains none of the goal, output name, input name, storage root, endpoint or key, and the Python writer rows that receipt; both IPC channels assert the sender, parse strictly and reuse the native save path; the workspace renders the section only for a submitted task when the bridge has the method, sends the exact payload, shows the recorded verdict and exports the receipt; the preload bridge exposes both methods on their channels; a version 3 task keeps its finish time across a verdict and receipts a declined consultation as `local-standard`.

Failures or blockers: None in the run. Not reproduced by a test: the `local-<profile>-consulted` arm, because no deterministic fixture settles a consultation.

Limitations and non-claims: Implemented, not Verified. No owner job has been rowed, no owner has recorded a verdict in the shipped build, no screenshot of the new section was taken, the Electron end-to-end suite was not run, and CI has not run on this branch. The tests prove the mechanics above and nothing about deliverable quality, OAJ or the owner's experience. `exportedThroughApp` is the owner's declaration, not a recorded export. `wallSeconds` on a desktop row is the task time the app shows (execution time on version 2 records, start to finish on version 3), not a harness wall clock. `git` on a superseding row is the writing commit, as the design entry decided, unlike the five hand-written superseding rows. The design entry's open points for the owner stand.

### BL-20261108-0911-probe-extensions-implemented -- 2026-11-08 -- Backlog item 5 implemented: probes P10, P11 and the adapter probe, the planner fixture, the role-schema export and assessor, and the serving-card writer

Status: `Implemented`

Scope or hypothesis: Backlog item 5 of docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.7, the prerequisite of E0 (section 5.6): extend `scripts/serving-probe.py` with probe P10 (structured output per role), probe P11 (prefill and decode by prompt size, cache reuse per extraction layout, K streams) and the adapter probe (`/openapi.json`, `/tokenize` parity, reasoning field, legacy or `flash_next_v1` consistency); add a planner fixture, a role-schema export with a reply assessor, and a serving-card writer, all tested offline. No persisted contract or dispatch semantics change, so no decision entry precedes this one.

Decisions: (1) The probe JSON is `probe_version` 2 with `probes_run`, `probes_skipped` and `probes_failed`, `--only` and `--skip` selection, lazy configuration (nothing reads the environment at import), a generic origin POST helper and a `keep_content` stream option; the address and the key are never printed or stored, and server error bodies are stored as status, length and sha256 only. The probe refuses a non-loopback base without `SOAR_VLLM_COST_POLICY=local_zero_cost` and also mirrors the app's insecure-HTTP rule (`vllmEndpointPolicyIssue` in config.ts), so it refuses exactly what the app refuses. (2) P10 classifies each reply in the order request_rejected, truncated, invalid_json, schema_invalid, binding_invalid (planner only), valid, with truncation counted apart from schema rejection, and records `reasoning_tokens` so grammar-suppressed thinking is visible. The language split: the probe retains each P10 reply body under the ignored run directory (mode 0600, sha256 in the JSON; `--strip-reasoning` drops reasoning fields) and `scripts/assess-probe-replies.ts` validates the retained replies with the real zod schemas (`assessResearchPlanReply`, `ExtractReplySchema`, `ResearchSynthesisSchema`) and writes the classification counts back; the role schemas, system prompts, output caps and synthetic payloads the probe sends come from `scripts/export-role-schemas.ts`, written to `.soar/experiments/role-schemas.json` and never committed. P10 records acceptance of both the `strict: true` variant (the ReviewResultV1 shape openai-compatible.ts already sends) and the non-strict variant with one call each, runs its 20-call cells on the requested variant when the server accepts it, and names the variant, so the card can say which one a 95% figure refers to. (3) P11 sizes synthetic documents at the measured 1.245 tokens per word, refuses a size whose prompt plus `max_tokens` exceeds P1's `max_model_len`, compares today's sorted-key extraction layout with the proposed `[system][stable packet][chunk]` layout under a fixed `cache_salt`, runs K in {1, 2, 4, 8} streams while sampling `vllm:num_requests_running`, and records counts, timings and digests only. (4) The adapter probe mirrors flash-next-reply.ts: the reasoning field name (none, reasoning, reasoning_content), `model` in JSON replies and SSE chunks, leading `<think>` leakage, reasoning under thinking off, and acceptance of `preserve_thinking` and `cache_salt`; it concludes consistency with the legacy shape and with `flash_next_v1`, never a verified contract. (5) The planner fixture (`scripts/planner-fixture.ts`) reads the endpoint through `loadConfig`, verifies the index, the brief and the source ids against the hashes-only manifest `docs/experiments/e0-planner-fixture-v1.json`, builds the pipeline's exact planner messages and vLLM body from the exported `PLAN_SYSTEM`, `OUTPUT_TOKENS` and the Heavy sampling, retains every raw reply under `.soar/experiments/e0-planner-fixture-<ts>/` (mode 0600) and writes attempt summaries holding codes, hashes and counts only. The committed manifest is a template with null hashes that the owner fills from the exposed r3 index; the fixture refuses a template or a mismatch before any request. The three conditions (legacy-thinking, flash-thinking, thinking-off) and the 3 x 10 design are proposals for the E0 card. (6) The probes and the fixture POST directly, outside the broker, by design: synthetic or public inputs at zero fee, no dispatch rows. (7) `scripts/serving-card.py` requires probe version 2 and prints the Source paragraph, the Identity table (alias, engine version, context, model root basename, authentication, transport class only), optional "consistent with the 2026-11-04 qualification" rows that never say "same weights", the Behaviour table including P10, P11 and the adapter probe, and a derived-bounds table (per role: output cap against the app's 300 s and 900 s clocks) marked as proposals for the E0 card; it refuses any string that looks like a URL, an IP address, a host:port or the configured endpoint's host, and never copies error detail fields.

Changes: scripts/serving-probe.py rewritten as per-probe functions; new scripts/export-role-schemas.ts, scripts/assess-probe-replies.ts, scripts/planner-fixture.ts, scripts/serving-card.py and docs/experiments/e0-planner-fixture-v1.json (template); src/main/private-agent/research-pipeline.ts exports PLAN_SYSTEM, EXTRACT_SYSTEM, SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM, OUTPUT_TOKENS, THINKING and ExtractReplySchema and adds RESEARCH_EXTRACT_JSON_SCHEMA, with no value changed; package.json gains probe:export-schemas, probe:assess, fixture:planner and card:serving; README.md's diagnostics list and docs/experiments/README.md document them; new tests tests/unit/serving-probe-helpers.test.ts, serving-card-writer.test.ts, planner-fixture.test.ts, role-schema-export.test.ts and assess-probe-replies.test.ts with tests/helpers/serving-probe-fixture.ts.

Evidence: Nothing ran against the endpoint: every test uses python3 -I with no SOAR variable set, a loopback fake server or synthetic JSON. `researchProtocolSha256()` is 3453710315d7226ea4d6195ec7401d000f86c5b0d9afa9839a801d5c6d391262 before (at 456344e) and after the exports, asserted in role-schema-export.test.ts. The offline tests prove: the probe's helpers import without an endpoint and classify, size, lay out, parse and aggregate as stated; the probe refuses before any socket without a base, without the cost policy on a non-loopback base, with an unknown probe name or without role schemas; error bodies reduce to length and digest; the fixture's bodies equal PrivateAgentModel's request bytes for all four conditions, its system message is PLAN_SYSTEM, its payload carries RESEARCH_PLAN_JSON_SCHEMA with repair null, replies are retained with mode 0600 and the summaries bind them by digest without the address, and a template or mismatched manifest refuses with zero requests; the export emits exactly the plan, extract and synthesis schemas equal to the TypeScript values; the assessor classifies retained replies in the probe's order and rewrites the counts; the card writer emits the tables, tells a skipped probe from a failed one, is deterministic, and refuses planted URLs, IPv4 and IPv6 literals, host:port strings, the configured host and a version 1 probe. The five new files pass (29 tests); `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3` passes 155 files and 2452 tests with 13 environment-gated files (81 tests) skipped; `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm validate:readiness` pass; `pnpm --silent validate:build-log -- --base-ref origin/claude/great-meitner-kri52m` reports a valid log with this entry appended.

Failures or blockers: None in the offline work. The committed planner-fixture manifest is a template, so E0's planner fixture cannot run until the owner fills its hashes from an exposed r3 index under `.soar` and sets its status to pinned. Open for the owner: which r3 index to pin, whether P10 and the fixture may retain reasoning text for synthetic and public inputs (`--strip-reasoning` exists), and whether the 95% rule binds the strict or the non-strict variant.

Limitations and non-claims: Nothing here measured the endpoint, and no live claim is made: the probes, the fixture, the assessor and the card writer are `Implemented`, not `Verified` against a server. The adapter probe shows consistency of a few synthetic replies with a reply contract, never the contract itself; the card's comparison rows show consistency with the 2026-11-04 qualification, never identical weights (owner decision 1 stays open). The derived bounds and the fixture's three conditions are proposals for the E0 card. The card writer's address patterns are a best effort, so the operator still reviews the card before commit. The harness source-freeze digest over `src/main/private-agent/*.ts` changes because of the exports; no loop is in flight, so nothing is invalidated. No persisted event, receipt, schema or dispatch rule changed.

Paid exposure: None. Zero model requests, zero endpoint requests and zero envelope spend. Every cap is unchanged.

Next gate: The reviewer opens the pull request from this branch. After merge, the E0 card names the P10 rule's variant and the fixture's conditions, the owner fills the planner-fixture manifest, and E0 runs from the owner's Mac at zero fee (docs/HANDOFF.md, "Start here", step 2).

### BL-20261108-1459-serving-card-reader-design -- 2026-11-08 -- Serving-card reader decided: the writer's machine-readable card, an env-pinned reader that reads only adopted cards and refuses every value no consumer reads yet, and the card's digest and copy in each run

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: This is the decision entry for SC, the shared serving-card reader in the plan for E1 and backlog items 6-11 charted under the wayfinder map (#46). It replaces three separate proposals in that plan with one contract:
- a card-contract change (a zod schema, plus the writer's JSON emission);
- a reader for item 7(a)'s caps and thinking and item 9's structured output;
- a numbers-only parameters file read through a `--serving-card` driver flag, for item 8's K.

It is recorded before its code because it adds a persisted input (the machine-readable serving card), two configuration variables, a freeze key and a file in each run directory. Review section 5.2, principle 6, re-derives every stage bound from the E0 serving card. Today no code reads a card: the writer prints only Markdown, the one committed card (2026-09-28) was written by hand, and E0's card does not exist yet. #57's step 4 must follow this change, because the card needs P1, P10, P11 and the adapter probe from one probe run. Based on `main` at 0e644e5. This is zero-fee code with deterministic tests and no endpoint, so it needs no approval under PLAN.md section 4(c). The implementation follows in the same pull request.

Decisions: (1) The card. `scripts/serving-card.py --policy-out <path>` writes a tracked JSON card, `docs/experiments/serving-card-<date>.json`, beside the Markdown card. It has `kind` "soar_serving_card", `version` 1 and exactly these keys:
- `date`;
- `decision` {`status` "proposed" or "adopted", `entry` a BL ID or null};
- `identity` {`servedModel`, `engineVersion`, `contextTokens`, `modelRootBasename`}, from probe P1;
- `probe` {`probeVersion` 2, `sha256` of the probe JSON the writer read, and the names of the probes run, skipped and failed};
- `roles`;
- `concurrency` {`localStreams`, K from 1 to 8};
- `admission` {`basis` "none" or "serving_card"};
- `evidence` {`p10`, `p11`, `bounds`, `adapter`}, each null when its probe did not run.

Each role has `maxOutputTokens` and `thinking` ("disabled" or "model"), each with exactly two entries: attempt 1, then attempt 2 (the repair or second call). Plan, extract and synthesis also have `structuredOutput`: null, or {`variant`, `thinkingOff`, `thinkingOn`} with at least one flag true.

P10 evidence holds:
- the calls per cell, the requested variant and each role's acceptance of both variants;
- the role export's protocol hash, the three schema digests, and the assessor's protocol hash and match, which must agree with the two hashes;
- for each cell, the variant it ran, its max_tokens, every class count (summing to the total), and the mean completion and reasoning tokens of settled replies. The writer computes the means because the probe records only medians.

P11 evidence holds:
- per prompt size: prompt and completion tokens, first-token time, the prefill and thinking-off decode rates, and tokens per word;
- the refused sizes;
- per extraction layout: cache-salt acceptance and each request's prompt tokens, cached tokens and first-token time, with the packet and chunk bytes;
- per K: streams, errors, median and aggregate decode, the maximum first-token and total times, and the running maximum.

`bounds` are the Markdown table's 300 s and 900 s ceilings. They may be zero or negative, and they are informational. `adapter` holds the two consistency verdicts and /tokenize parity. Every object is strict and every key is present, null where a value is absent. The card never holds an address, a path, a key, a timestamp other than its date, or reply text.

(2) The writer.
- For both outputs, it refuses (exit 2, nothing printed) a served alias or engine version that looks like a file path. The message names only the JSON path and asks for `--served-model-name`. For every other input the base writer accepted, the Markdown is byte-identical with or without the flag.
- `--policy-out` is refused when:
  - P1 does not give exactly one served alias;
  - the role export's caps and thinking are missing;
  - the date is not valid;
  - the probe exceeds the card's list bounds; or
  - the file already exists.
- It runs `refuse_addresses` over the JSON and encodes both outputs before creating the file, with O_EXCL. It removes the file on any later failure, including a failed Markdown write, and never prints the path.
- It writes `decision` {"proposed", null} and proposes:
  - caps and thinking as the role export sent them;
  - structured output for a role and thinking mode only when P10 was assessed under the protocol it sent, and the cell ran the requested variant with no unassessed reply, at least 20 calls and at least 95% valid;
  - `localStreams` 1;
  - admission "none".

(3) Selection. `SOAR_SERVING_CARD_FILE` (an absolute path without control characters) and `SOAR_SERVING_CARD_SHA256` (64 lowercase hexadecimal characters) must be set together or not at all. config.ts validates them like the token-admission pair, but without its flash_next_v1 requirement, and produces `config.vllm.servingCard` only when both are set. Both live in the ignored `.env.local`. There is no driver flag and no separate parameters file.

(4) The reader. The new `src/main/private-agent/serving-card.ts` comes with two leaf modules: `research-roles.ts` (the role policy schema, defaults equal to today's OUTPUT_TOKENS and THINKING, and the shared non-default predicate) and `serving-card-flags.ts` (the consumed flags). It checks in this order:
- The pinned read uses flash-next-admission.ts's `pinned`, now exported and opened with O_NONBLOCK, so a FIFO is refused instead of blocking. It requires an absolute path, no symlink, a regular file of at most 64 KiB, no change during the read and an equal sha256, else `serving_card_pin_drift`.
- UTF-8 JSON of kind "soar_serving_card": another version gives `serving_card_version_unsupported`; anything else that fails the strict schema, a path-like alias included, gives `serving_card_invalid`.
- Status "adopted" with an entry, else `serving_card_not_adopted`.
- `servedModel` equal to SOAR_VLLM_MODEL, else `serving_card_model_mismatch`.
- Under flash_next_v1, `contextTokens` equal to SOAR_VLLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS, else `serving_card_context_mismatch`.
- Every cap between 128 and 16,384, else `serving_card_cap_out_of_range`; it is refused, never clamped. 16,384 is the heavy profile's limit, and every research role runs under heavy: the driver refuses the pipeline, a seeded run and the loop under any other profile.
- For every flagged structured-output mode:
  - an assessed P10, else `serving_card_structured_output_unassessed`;
  - the export's and the assessor's protocol hashes equal to today's `researchProtocolSha256()`, else `serving_card_p10_protocol_drift`;
  - the role's schema digest equal to sha256(canonical(current role schema)), else `serving_card_schema_drift`;
  - the cell present with no unassessed reply, else `serving_card_structured_output_unassessed`;
  - the flag's variant equal to the requested variant and to the cell's, else `serving_card_structured_output_variant_mismatch`;
  - at least 20 calls and at least 95% valid, else `serving_card_structured_output_below_rule`.
- K above 1 only with a P11 burst at that K with K streams and zero errors, else `serving_card_streams_unproven`.

Each refusal is a `ServingCardError` whose message is its code. The three file-level codes carry no key path. The others carry one fixed key path from an exported allowlist, never card text, a card key or the file path. The resolver has no override argument; tests flip flags only by mocking the flags module.

(5) Fail closed. After those checks, any value that differs from today's default is refused with `serving_card_parameter_unconsumed` until its consumer flips its flag. Such values are a role's caps or thinking on either attempt, a non-null structured output, K other than 1, or admission other than "none".
- The flags are flipped as follows: `maxOutputTokens` and `thinking` by item 7(a)'s caps-and-thinking PR, `structuredOutput` by item 9, `localStreams` by item 8's loop PR, and `admission` by item 7(b)'s admission PR.
- All five are false here, so an adopted all-default card is accepted and any other adopted card is refused.
- Effective values come only from the resolved policy. A consumer reads evidence only to refuse, or under a policy value that its flag guards; item 7(b) reads it only when the admission basis is "serving_card".
- Item 7(a)'s hash binding and this gate share one role-level predicate.

(6) Defaults. Without the pair nothing reads a file, and the policy is today's caps and thinking on both attempts, no structured output, K 1 and admission "none".

(7) The driver. scripts/private-agent-local-screen.ts loads the card right after its provider check, before the run directory, the database or any request exists, so a refusal leaves nothing behind and a loop stays resumable. When a card is set, it:
- saves the pinned bytes as serving-card.json (wx, 0600) beside freeze.json;
- adds a top-level `servingCard` {sha256, version, date, entry} to freeze.json, never the path;
- on a card refusal, adds the refusal's code and key path to the existing failure line.

An optional second argument passes configuration options to loadConfig, so tests never read the repository's `.env.local`; the CLI and the loop never pass it. Nothing else consumes the card: the session, the pipeline, the model configurations, phase2-repair's critic and the desktop read nothing.

(8) Byte identity. Without a card, the following stay as they are:
- every request body;
- every model and session identity;
- `researchProtocolSha256()` (3453710315d7226ea4d6195ec7401d000f86c5b0d9afa9839a801d5c6d391262 at 0e644e5), with both pins untouched and no new test pinning it;
- loadConfig's result;
- the freeze, except the source-freeze digests.

With a card, only freeze.json (and so result.json's `freezeSha256`) differs, plus the copy in the run directory. The `pinned` change alters only non-regular files: they are now refused instead of blocking.

(9) Owner defaults recorded here.
- Only adopted cards are read. `decision.entry` names the BL entry that records E0's result, set only once that entry's ID is final on main; its format is checked, not its presence in this ledger.
- P10 evidence is bound to the whole default protocol hash.
- The card records the variant P10 ran, which is the requested variant unless the server refused it. Structured output is proposed and accepted only on the requested variant: strict by default, the probe's default.
- A cap above the heavy limit is refused, not clamped.
- Refreshing any evidence means re-running P1, P10, P11 and the adapter together and adopting a new card.

Changes: Planned in this pull request:
- scripts/serving-card.py: `--policy-out`, the JSON builder, the path-like identity refusal, and a ceiling helper the Markdown table shares unchanged.
- New src/main/private-agent/research-roles.ts, serving-card-flags.ts and serving-card.ts.
- src/main/private-agent/flash-next-admission.ts: `pinned` exported and opened with O_NONBLOCK.
- src/main/config.ts: the pair and `vllm.servingCard`.
- scripts/private-agent-local-screen.ts: `buildLocalScreenServingCard`, the optional configuration argument, the load, the run-directory copy, the freeze key and the catch.
- .env.example, README.md and docs/experiments/README.md.
- Tests:
  - extended: serving-card-writer.test.ts, config.test.ts, private-agent-local-role-config.test.ts and phase4-loop.test.ts (one appended test);
  - new: serving-card-reader.test.ts, serving-card-reader-consumed.test.ts and tests/helpers/serving-card-fixture.ts;
  - tests/integration/private-agent-runtime.test.ts (Docker-gated): its configuration is passed explicitly, plus one case with a card.

Evidence: None yet; this entry decides. Three adversarial design reviews (contract and privacy, consumers and tests, spec fidelity) checked the design against the code at 0e644e5 and raised 22 findings, five of them major. Each was checked against the code and confirmed.

Applied:
- the writer refuses a file-path-like served alias (1);
- no consumed-flag override, a leaf flags module, and a loaded card that exposes the policy, never the raw values (2);
- encode-before-create JSON writing with cleanup and no path in messages (3);
- `probe.sha256` (4);
- the run-directory copy (5);
- the key-path allowlist (6);
- O_NONBLOCK in `pinned` (7);
- P10 evidence bound to today's protocol hash (8);
- the configuration argument for driver tests (9);
- writer-to-reader round trips on edge-case probes, with negative ceilings allowed (10);
- caps bounded by the heavy profile without a default exemption (11, 18);
- a Docker-gated freeze-placement case and a loop-record test (12, in part);
- the shared role predicate (13);
- the full re-probe rule (14);
- `maxTotalS` and the short-prompt limitation (15, in part);
- no third protocol-hash pin (16, 19);
- the requested-variant rule (17);
- the gates' limits stated (20);
- the #57 constraints (21);
- traceable references (22).

Not applied:
- a pure freeze-builder refactor (12): it would turn the plan's trivial overlap with item 11's freeze change into a refactor conflict;
- per-burst prompt tokens (15): probe version 2 does not record them.

Reproduced in a scratch directory, outside the repository:
- a served alias `/home/<user>/models/...` passes `refuse_addresses` and is printed in the Markdown;
- under Python 3.9.5, `open(path, "x", encoding="utf-8")` leaves a 0-byte file when a lone surrogate fails to encode;
- under Node 22.22.2, the pinned read's open blocks on a FIFO until a 3 s alarm, while with O_NONBLOCK the FIFO is refused as not a regular file.

The design rests on a reading of the code at 0e644e5:
- the token-admission pair and its pinned read (config.ts:48-49 and :98-105; flash-next-admission.ts:54-66);
- loadConfig's file loading (config.ts:182-208);
- OUTPUT_TOKENS, THINKING and the protocol hash (research-pipeline.ts:28-29 and :75-81);
- two attempts per role unit (research-contract.ts:8 and :11);
- the profiles' limits, the clamp at model.ts:337, and the heavy-only research paths (private-agent-local-screen.ts:278, :465 and :473; phase4-loop.ts:90);
- the probe's P1, P10 and P11 records, including the variant fallback at serving-probe.py:361-368 and the bursts' one-sentence prompt (:802, :928);
- the assessor's one-time `schemasProtocolMatch` (assess-probe-replies.ts:80-81);
- the driver's config load, directory creation, snapshot copies, token-admission load and freeze (private-agent-local-screen.ts:302-312, :323 and :372-391);
- the freeze readers, which read fields one by one.

Running the base writer under python3 -I on the test fixture syntheticProbe() gives Markdown sha256 5cf363caa1c6d62bc2719501979a9056569f21c394afaac806f86ba12536f426 (9,024 bytes) with the three comparison flags, and b0278fa07d79e4db737eb6f85bae061521c2c11667969175d038055edd25b5d4 (8,508 bytes) without them; the writer test will pin both. In that fixture, plan/on (19/20), extract/on and extract/off (20/20) and synthesis/off (19/20) meet the 95% rule, while plan/off (17/20) and synthesis/on (18/20) do not.

Failures or blockers: None in recording. Open for the owner, with none blocking the code:
- whether `admission.basis` is the value item 7(b)'s admission flag guards;
- whether per-attempt values take exactly two entries;
- whether P10 evidence stays bound to the whole default protocol hash (the default here) or only to the role schema digests;
- whether the writer proposes structured output by the 95% rule or leaves every proposal at its default;
- whether a refresh may merge P10 from a second probe run instead of a full re-probe; that would need per-block provenance and a card version 2;
- whether the reader should also refuse a flash_next_v1 configuration against a card whose adapter probe was not consistent with that contract.

Limitations and non-claims: This entry decides; nothing is implemented, verified or released by it, and no serving card exists until E0 (#57).

Until items 7(a), 9, 8 and 7(b) merge their PRs:
- an adopted E0 card with any proposed non-default value is refused, and a refused card stops every driver run while the pair is set;
- only an all-default card is usable, and it changes nothing but the freeze and the run-directory copy;
- after E0, a PR that changes `researchProtocolSha256()`'s default (items 7(c) and 7(b) in the plan) leaves structured output refused until a full re-probe and a new adopted card.

The gates check the card, not the measurement:
- The identity check compares the served alias and, under flash_next_v1, the context. It cannot establish identical weights or the engine version, and owner decision 1 stays open.
- The evidence numbers are the writer's copy of a probe JSON kept under the ignored `.soar/`. `probe.sha256` lets a reviewer re-run the writer and compare, but the gates check only the card's internal consistency.
- P10's thinking-off cells send the probe's own sampling, non-streaming and without preserve_thinking, so a passing cell does not show that the pipeline's own requests are at least 95% valid (P10-align is still open on #47).
- The unchanged Markdown verdict has no 20-call minimum and ignores the protocol match, so it can say "meets" where the JSON proposes null.

### BL-20261108-1649-serving-card-reader-implemented -- 2026-11-08 -- Serving-card reader implemented: the writer's machine-readable card, the env-pinned fail-closed reader, the run record, and the code-review fixes

Status: `Implemented`

Scope or hypothesis: SC, the shared serving-card reader decided in BL-20261108-1459-serving-card-reader-design, implemented on `feat/sc-serving-card-reader` from `main` at 0e644e5: 86d2b81 implements the design, and 8de520b applies the findings of one code review of 86d2b81. This is zero-fee code with deterministic tests; nothing touched the endpoint. The design entry's decisions (1)-(9) stand. The decisions below record only details fixed in code that extend them or that the design left open.

Decisions: (1) The writer. Extending design decision (2), `--policy-out` also refuses:
- a model root basename that is not a plain file name (a slash, a backslash, a control character or more than 256 UTF-16 code units), so the writer never writes a card its own reader would reject;
- a `P10.assessed` whose `schemasProtocolMatch` disagrees with the export's and the assessor's protocol hashes;
- a structurally malformed probe record, named by a fixed JSON path, never by its value;
- a JSON card over 64 KiB;
- a lone surrogate or a non-finite number, with a fixed message that never echoes the character.

Further writer details:
- A wrong-typed, negative or non-finite measurement becomes null. An empty engine version becomes null, matching the Markdown's "version not read", and so does an empty root basename.
- Records are written in a fixed order: cells by role then thinking on/off, sizes and K numerically, layouts by name.
- The writer drops one leading `--`, with or without `--policy-out`. pnpm 10 passes it through from `pnpm card:serving -- ...`, and argparse read every flag after it as a positional. The parser has no positional, so no invocation that worked before changes.

(2) The reader. Extending design decision (4):
- A `__proto__` key (zod 4 drops it silently) and a key repeated within one object (JSON.parse keeps only the last value) are `serving_card_invalid`. The resolved card, a top-down reading of the file and the bytes copied into the run directory therefore agree. Keys are compared after unescaping.
- `serving_card_version_unsupported` needs kind "soar_serving_card" and a numeric version other than 1; a missing version is `serving_card_invalid`.
- Identity strings refuse lone surrogates, and the date refuses the year 0000.

(3) Key paths.
- An unconsumed value carries `roles.<role>.<parameter>`, `concurrency.localStreams` or `admission.basis`.
- A cap refusal adds `[0]` or `[1]`; a structured-output gate adds `.thinkingOff` or `.thinkingOn`.
- The allowlist is a frozen array behind a module-private lookup, `isServingCardParameterPath`. `ServingCardError` drops any other key path. `servingCardRefusal` checks the code and the key path again before any failure line prints them.

(4) Failure lines.
- The driver's CLI line comes from `localScreenFailureLine`. A refusal adds `code` and, except for the three file-level codes, `parameter`; every other failure prints the bytes it printed at 0e644e5.
- Extending design decision (7), the loop's `log.txt`, `errors.txt` and CLI line (`loopFailureLine`) also name the key path; `loop.json` keeps the code only. Without a refusal, each loop line keeps its earlier bytes.

(5) A guard test (R10) fails when any module under src/ or scripts/ other than serving-card.ts names `parseServingCard` or `ServingCardV1Schema`, or reads `vllm.servingCard` outside `buildLocalScreenServingCard`. A consumer therefore reads values only through the pinned, adopted, fail-closed load.

### BL-20261109-0331-loop-selection-protocol-2-design -- 2026-11-09 -- Backlog item 11, part 1 decided: selection protocol 2 (the original wins ties, the entailment step decides nothing), the harness loop admitting resolved zero-fee failed rows, and the loop's interrupt and identity guards

Status: `Proposed`

Scope or hypothesis: The decision entry for the first part of backlog item 11 of docs/PROJECT_REVIEW_2026-11-05.md section 5.7 (plan ID 11.1, in issue #46's lane C), recorded before its code because it changes the selection methodology (a persisted protocol version and what `loop.json`'s and the registry's `step` can say), the harness loop's dispatch stop rule and resume rules, and the registry's columns. It covers three of item 11's clauses: "ties to the original, reversing the recorded preference (finding E9)" (section 5.2, S11); "the entailment step off unless E0's judge fixture reaches its agreement level and graded runs show the rate separating accepted from rejected drafts (finding E10)" (S10); and "the loop's stage checks (`phase4-loop.ts:139-140`, now :155-156) admitting a zero-fee `failed` row that its stage resolved (item 1)". Two guards the reviews showed the third clause needs come with it: a stage cut by the loop's own interrupt is never reused as a candidate, and a loop is never resumed under another runtime or protocol. For every loop started under the new protocol it supersedes step (4) and the repair half of step (5) of BL-20261026-1831-h4-select-and-repair-design (sample `a` over `b` stays), and, for zero-fee failed rows only, the stop "when a dispatch is UNKNOWN, committed/unresolved, or failed" of BL-20261101-0436-h4-runner-controls-fixed and docs/plans/PHASE4_LOOP_DISPATCH_STOP_V1.md; those records stay as written and loops recorded under protocol 1 keep their meaning. The rest of item 11 (the run's commit in `git`, `infra_invalid` classification with one zero-fee resume, the new registry columns, the launcher, gate signals, paired retrieval) is decided by later entries. It reads no serving card and needs none. It is zero-fee code with deterministic tests and needs no approval under PLAN.md section 4(c); the owner may record otherwise.

Decisions: (1) **Selection protocol 2, ties to the original (finding E9).** `SELECTION_PROTOCOL_VERSION` becomes 2 (src/main/private-agent/selection.ts) and is carried as before in `loop.json` `selectionRule` and the registry's `loop.rule`. `compareCandidates(first, second)` keeps its contract that the caller's `first` wins every tie. Stage 1 stays `compareCandidates(a, b)`, so sample `a` keeps a tie against `b`, as under protocol 1. Stage 2 becomes `compareCandidates(selected, repair)`, so the selected draft keeps a tie against its repair: the repair is chosen only when it is submitted and the draft is not, when it passes more critical checks verified on its final snapshot, or when it has more deliverables present. `entailmentRates` follows the comparison's order in both stages, [incumbent, challenger]: stage 1 records [a, b] as before, and stage 2 records [selected draft, repair], the reverse of protocol 1's stage-2 order [repair, draft]. Only tests read the rates (scripts/registry-row.py reads the stage-1 candidate and the final candidate and step); a consumer takes the order from `selectionRule`. (2) **The entailment step decides nothing (finding E10).** Protocol 2's steps are submission, critical checks, deliverables present, then the tie. The balance rate is computed exactly as before (`entailmentRate`: null for a missing or truncated pass or below ENTAILMENT_MIN_JUDGED, 10 judged claims) and recorded in `entailmentRates` as evidence only. No flag, option or serving-card value turns a judge step back on in selection. Turning one on is a later protocol bump under its own entry, which names E0's judge-fixture result against the agreement level E0's card sets and graded runs showing the rate separating accepted from rejected drafts; finding F8 found neither the support rate nor the balance rate separating them. ENTAILMENT_MIN_MARGIN (0.10), which only step (4) used, is removed, and so is the `SelectionStep` value `entailment`. A protocol-2 `step` is therefore `submitted`, `checks`, `artifacts` or `tie`, besides the loop's own ends (`stage_failed`, `no_draft`, `critique_failed`); `entailment` appears only in protocol-1 records and in registry rows with `loop.rule` 1. This concerns selection only: criterion 8's entailment threshold, which E0 may activate for E3 and E4 (review section 2.2), is an acceptance criterion this part does not touch, so a loop may keep a tied draft that fails criterion 8 over a repair that passes it. (3) **The stop rule admits resolved zero-fee failed rows.** A dispatch row in a stage's `result.json` is a zero-fee failed row when all of these hold: its status is `failed`; it is not an assist row (item 10's two purposes, counted apart already); its `destinationId` is a string in an allowlist of the two harness destinations that never carry a fee, `owned_local_model` (the owned local model at zero prices) and `approved_public_snapshots` (the loopback public-snapshot fixture, reached by GET); its `reservedFeeMicrousd` is a JSON number equal to 0 (never a boolean or a string); it has no `feeMicrousd` key, or one equal to the number 0 (a null fails closed); and it has no `approval` key at all (a null fails closed). Any missing or malformed field fails closed. The allowlist (`ZERO_FEE_DESTINATIONS` in selection.ts, mirrored in scripts/registry-row.py and checked against the driver's destination ids by a test) excludes `cloud_coordinator` by construction, including under a zero-price cloud arm (`parseCloudPrices` admits 0), and stops the loop on any destination added later until an entry names it. The receipt records no destination kind, method or grant, so the predicate rests on the driver's three destinations; it is a superset of the broker's zero-risk set only for a grant-backed row without an approval, which no code mints today (consultation grants always carry an approval), and a row that is not zero-risk resolves `failed` only on `connection_failed` or `http_rejected`, which sent nothing that executed. Such a row reserved nothing, settled nothing and leaves nothing pending: `failed` rows add 0 to the store's exposure. Zero-risk rows have resolved `failed` on every transport and settlement diagnostic since backlog item 1, and on `connection_failed`, `http_rejected` and a public GET's non-2xx answer before it. The stage that made the row handled it: a failed reading-stage call ends the reading stage, so no evidence packet coexists with a failed reader row (BL-20261107-0809); a failed public fetch reaches the writer as `public_fetch_failed` and the task continues; a failed judge call stops only the entailment pass; a failed writer call ends the run (`model_unavailable`, or `cancelled_or_deadline` under a cancel or the deadline). `summarizeRun` reports `zeroFeeFailedDispatches` as a subset of `failedDispatches`, which keeps its meaning, every non-assist `failed` row. The loop's stage check throws `loop_stage_failed_dispatch` unless `failedDispatches` equals `zeroFeeFailedDispatches`, so a missing or inconsistent count also stops it. These still stop the loop: a priced failed row, such as a cloud call refused with a 4xx; a row to the cloud destination at any reservation; a row with an approval; a `failed` row whose reservation is missing, as in hand-made fixtures; every `committed` row; and every non-assist `unknown` row. (4) **What an admitted row leads to.** The sample is an ordinary candidate. A zero-fee failure in sample `a`'s reading stage ends that stage without a packet, so the loop ends at `stage_failed` with the seed loader's refusal code (item 4's `seedRefusal`) and has a final selection. Today such a loop throws and is left without one, and the registry writer refuses to row it (finding E1). A zero-fee failure in a write phase leaves an incomplete or submitted candidate, which steps (1) to (3) compare. A sample that ended for an infrastructural reason (the endpoint down, `model_unavailable`) is therefore evaluated as an ordinary incomplete candidate, and a loop whose sample `a` lost its reading stage that way is terminal, until part 3 (11.3) classifies such ends `infra_invalid` and resumes them once at zero fee. Part 3 must merge before any graded loop run (E3; E6's review-2 arm, which is this loop). (5) **A stage the loop's own interrupt cut is never reused as a candidate.** The driver handles the signal too, so an interrupt cancels the running stage: its in-flight zero-fee request resolves `failed` (code `cancelled`) and it ends `cancelled_or_deadline`, or `research_cancelled` in the reading stage; and the session deadline produces the same codes. So the loop marks the stage it was running when its own interrupt fired (`interrupted: true` on the stage's `loop.json` entry, carried onto every later reuse of that stage and dropped once the stage runs afresh). A later invocation refuses to reuse a marked candidate stage (`a`, `b` or the repair) that did not submit, with `loop_stage_interrupted`, after its dispatch checks; the operator moves it aside and the loop reruns it, as for an unfinished stage, until part 3 automates the zero-fee case. A marked stage that submitted is complete and is reused. This closes a gap older than this part: a stage cut between two requests holds no failed row and is reused as an ordinary candidate today (a reading stage cut that way ends the loop at `stage_failed`); with (3) a cut that catches a request in flight would join it. A stage cut by the session deadline is not marked and stays an ordinary candidate. (6) **No loop is resumed under another runtime or protocol.** Before it touches the loop directory, the loop computes the live source freeze (`localScreenSourceFreeze()`, an injectable dependency) and refuses with `loop_reviewed_source_changed` unless it equals `--runtime-sha256`; today only the driver checks the live source, and a reused stage never calls the driver, so a stale `--runtime-sha256` let a loop whose remaining stages were all on disk finish under new code. A prior `loop.json` whose `version`, `selectionRule`, `runtimeSha256`, `task`, `arm` or `pipeline` differs from the invocation's is refused with `loop_record_mismatch` before any stage and is left as it was. So no protocol-1 loop is finished under protocol 2, whatever hash the operator passes. (7) **Counts.** `CandidateSummary` gains `zeroFeeFailedDispatches`, and the loop's `totals` gain the same key; the totals type is derived from TOTAL_KEYS. The key is additive, so LOOP_VERSION stays 1, as item 10 kept it for its two columns. scripts/registry-row.py adds the column to `run_counts` and `SUMMED` with the same predicate, so `--run-dir` and `--loop-dir` rows (summed over the loop's runs) carry it. docs/experiments/README.md documents it in its own row beside the dispatch columns: rows written before this change, desktop verdict-receipt rows and `--supersedes` copies of earlier rows omit it, and an absent column does not mean 0. It also documents `loop.rule` 1 against 2 in its own paragraph, so consumers can split old loop rows from new ones: under rule 1, stage-2 ties went to the repair, `step` could be `entailment`, and any failed row stopped the loop, so every rule-1 loop row carries `failedDispatches` 0; under rule 2, ties keep the original, the rates decide nothing, and a loop row may carry zero-fee failed rows. The TypeScript predicate and its Python mirror are tested on the same fixture rows, including `false`, `null`, `0.0` and `"0"` values. The desktop verdict receipt is unchanged (`VERDICT_RECEIPT_KEYS` and `RECEIPT_KEYS`). (8) **Not in this part.** No one-sample loop mode (`--samples 1`) is added: E3's card (issue #63) has not raised the question (see (b) below). Passing the loop's interrupt signal to the critique (E1's bug d) is part 3. No serving-card value is read. (9) **Runtime identity.** selection.ts and scripts/phase4-loop.ts are inside `localScreenSourceFreeze`, so this change rotates the runtime hash: the driver's freeze keeps its shape, while its `sourceFreeze` values and `sourceFreezeSha256` change. No loop is in flight, and (6) refuses any loop started before the merge. `researchProtocolSha256()`, every request body, and the packet and destination identities pinned by tests/unit/private-agent-identity-golden.test.ts are unchanged.

Open owner questions, with the proposed defaults this entry records (this entry does not answer them for the owner): (a) Findings E9 and E10: may selection protocol 2 give ties to the original and drop the entailment step from every loop by default, keeping the balance rate as recorded evidence, and may turning a judge step back on require a later protocol bump whose entry names E0's judge-fixture result and the graded-run separation? Proposed default: yes to both, as backlog item 11 specifies; protocol 2 has no entailment step and no flag to enable one. (b) For E3's card (issue #63, where it is not yet raised) and E4's: should each arm run as the two-sample loop (a, b, critique, repair) or as one sample with one critique and repair? Proposed default: one sample, as v5's S8 (one write) and S11 (one round) specify, through a small `--samples 1` mode added in its own pull request only on the owner's yes; this entry adds none, and E6's review-2 arm keeps two samples. (c) Under protocol 2 a repair can change the outcome only when the selected draft did not submit: a submitted draft passes every critical check and has every deliverable, so its repair can at best tie, is never selected, and still costs the critique's and the repair's wall time (criterion 7). Should the loop skip the critique and repair when the stage-1 draft submitted? Proposed default: not now; E3's and E6's rows record each such case (a loop row whose stage-1 draft submitted, in `loop.candidates`, with `repaired` true), and skipping would be a later lever under its own entry. (d) The only measurement bearing on the tie rule favours the repair (see Limitations): keep ties to the original anyway? Proposed default: yes, as specified, and the E3 and E6 cards pre-register blind grades of both candidates in every repaired loop whose stage-1 draft submitted, so the rule itself is measured.
